title: Unknown-attribute lookup on streamlit imports modules since 1.65 (breaks iteration over sys.modules)
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

### Summary

Since 1.65.0, looking up any unknown attribute on the `streamlit` module (even `hasattr(st, "x")` or `getattr(st, "x", None)`) imports `streamlit.command_suggestions` and `difflib`. Code that iterates over `sys.modules` while probing module attributes then fails with `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`. This broke our whole test suite at setup after upgrading from 1.64.0.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import sys
import streamlit

[m for m in sys.modules.values() if getattr(m, "date", None) is not None]
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the script above in a fresh interpreter with streamlit 1.65.0.

### Expected Behavior

As in 1.64.0: the lookup returns the default, and no module is imported.

### Current Behavior

```
RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration
```

The module `__getattr__` added in #16912 imports `streamlit.command_suggestions` on every miss, including lookups that only probe with a default:

```python
import sys, streamlit
before = set(sys.modules)
hasattr(streamlit, "date")                 # False, as expected
print(sorted(set(sys.modules) - before))   # ['difflib', 'streamlit.command_suggestions']
```

### Is this a regression?

Yes, this used to work in a previous version (1.64.0).

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0
- Python version: 3.14.3
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: n/a

### Additional Information

The pattern is common in test suites: a pytest fixture scans the loaded modules to patch a name (here, freezing `date.today()`). We have fixed our side by iterating over `list(sys.modules.values())`, since iterating over the live dict is fragile in general. But a plain `hasattr` or `getattr(..., default)` now has an import side effect. Some possible ways to avoid it:

- import `streamlit.command_suggestions` eagerly (or once, at first use outside `__getattr__`);
- only build suggestions when the `AttributeError` is actually raised to user code, not on probes;
- or document that unknown-attribute lookups import modules.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

_No response_

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

related_pr.title: [fix] st attribute probes no longer import modules
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Looking up a missing `st.*` name with `hasattr` or `getattr(..., default)` no longer imports `streamlit.command_suggestions` or `difflib`. Those imports changed `sys.modules` during iteration and raised `RuntimeError`.

Suggestion text is still built when the `AttributeError` is displayed. `from streamlit import missing` stays a plain `ImportError` without a suggestion, because import machinery does not format the underlying error.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #17298

## Testing Plan

E2E coverage is omitted because this is an import side effect of attribute probes, with no UI path.

title: Tooltips render far above the hovered element in 1.65.0
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

Starting in 1.65.0, pydeck tooltips appear far above the hovered object, often off-screen.
The same app works correctly on 1.64.0.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pydeck as pdk
import streamlit as st

st.write(f"Streamlit {st.__version__}")

data = [{"position": [-98.35, 39.5], "name": "Test point"}]

st.pydeck_chart(
    pdk.Deck(
        initial_view_state=pdk.ViewState(latitude=39.5, longitude=-98.35, zoom=4),
        layers=[pdk.Layer("ScatterplotLayer", data, pickable=True, get_position="position",
                          get_fill_color=[255, 0, 0], radius_min_pixels=10)],
        tooltip={"text": "{name}"},
    )
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the app with streamlit==1.65.0.
Hover over the red dot.

### Expected Behavior

Tooltip appears next to the cursor, as it does in 1.64.0.

### Current Behavior

Tooltip appears offset far above the cursor, often off-screen.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0 (bug), 1.64.0 (works)
- Python version: 3.13
- pydeck 0.9.3
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Safari version 27

### Additional Information

Possibly related: 1.65.0 changed st.pydeck_chart (new alt parameter, PR #17086).
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #17313: [fix] Align pydeck tooltips with the cursor.

related_pr.title: [fix] Align pydeck tooltips with the cursor
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Pydeck tooltips sit on the cursor again. deck.gl 9.4 places them by subtracting `.deck-widgets-root` from the canvas, and that root was laid out one chart height below the map, so the tooltip rendered above the pointer.

The chart container stretches `.deck-widgets-root` over the canvas (`position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none`). Those are the same properties as the deck.gl fix that is merged but not in a release yet ([visgl/deck.gl#10724](https://github.com/visgl/deck.gl/pull/10724)). Downgrading `@deck.gl/*` from 9.4.0 to 9.3.11 would drop the rest of the 9.4 fixes, and pinning only core or only react breaks their peer ranges. The rule does not use `!important`, so the same inline styles win when they ship.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #17309

## Testing Plan

- No frontend unit test: jsdom's mocked DeckGL never mounts `.deck-widgets-root`, so it cannot reproduce the offset.

- Manual: default height, `height=250`, `height="stretch"`, and fullscreen all kept the tooltip on the cursor. Pan and Mapbox zoom still receive clicks.

title: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

AppTest loses a conditional text input's value when it is hidden and shown again with `persist_state="page"`, although the test never switches pages. The same sequence retains the value in a browser, and `persist_state="session"` works in AppTest.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

if st.toggle("Show", key="show"):
    st.text_input("SKU", key="sku", persist_state="page")
""").run()

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
at.text_input[0].set_value("SKU-42").run()
at.toggle[0].set_value(False).run()
print("While hidden:", repr(at.session_state["sku"]))
assert at.session_state["sku"] == "SKU-42"

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
print("After showing again:", repr(at.text_input[0].value))
assert not at.exception
assert at.text_input[0].value == "SKU-42"  # Fails: actual value is "".
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install Streamlit 1.65.0 in a normal Python environment: `pip install streamlit==1.65.0`.
2. Save the example as `repro_page_persistence.py` and run `python repro_page_persistence.py`. Pytest is not required.
3. Observe that the hidden value is still `SKU-42`, but the final input value is empty and the final assertion fails.
4. Change `persist_state="page"` to `persist_state="session"` and run again. The value remains `SKU-42` and the assertion passes.
5. For a browser comparison, save only the app string as `app.py`, run `streamlit run app.py`, enable Show, enter `SKU-42` and press Enter, then disable and re-enable Show. The browser retains the input value.

### Expected Behavior

Page-scoped persistence should keep the value through the hide/show sequence in AppTest because the test remains on the same page. It should return `SKU-42` after the input is shown again, matching the browser.

### Current Behavior

Reproduced on both Streamlit 1.64.0 and 1.65.0:

```text
While hidden: 'SKU-42'
After showing again: ''
AssertionError
```

There are no application exceptions in `at.exception`; the failure is the final test assertion. A browser comparison on both versions retains `SKU-42`. AppTest's `persist_state="session"` control also retains it; the default `persist_state=None` control resets it as expected.

### Is this a regression?

A previously working version has not been established. The versions tested are 1.64.0 and 1.65.0.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0; also reproduced on 1.64.0.
- Python version: 3.14.8.
- Operating System: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Browser: Not required for the AppTest reproduction. Browser comparisons used the Codex in-app browser on macOS.
- Package integrity: The tested Streamlit Python files match their wheel RECORD hashes. No installed Streamlit source was modified.

### Additional Information

#### Related issues checked

- [#17119](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17119) concerns the remount of a `persist_state=None` widget and a backend/frontend mismatch. This reproduction uses explicit page persistence and works in a browser.
- [#17093](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17093) concerns a delayed first mount after a session-state value was set. Here, the widget was mounted, edited, hidden, and remounted.
- [#16611](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16611) concerns `AppTest.switch_page()` with a custom `url_path`. This example has no page switch or custom URL path.
- [#9128](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9128) and [#12566](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12566) report KeyErrors with changing widget trees. This example has no script exception and loses a page-persistent value.

I did not find an existing issue with this same reproduction.

#### Possible cause

AppTest creates a fresh PagesManager for each run. Its current page hash initially equals `""`. ScriptRunner interprets the mismatch with the target page hash as a page change and performs cleanup before resetting the context, so page-scoped persistence can be evaluated against the empty current hash.

Source links are pinned to the inspected develop commit `ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e`:

- [AppTest creates PagesManager](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py#L506).
- [PagesManager initializes an empty current page hash](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/pages_manager.py#L50).
- [ScriptRunner performs page-change cleanup before context reset](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py#L660).

In a separate single-page diagnostic on both released versions, seeding the reconstructed runner's current page hash with the main page hash before cleanup makes this reproduction pass. It also prevents a keyed stateful tab from resetting after a child-widget interaction in AppTest. This diagnostic is evidence about the cleanup path; a complete fix must still handle real page switches correctly. The develop source was inspected, not executed.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #17305: [fix] Keep AppTest page widget state on rerun.

related_pr.title: [fix] Keep AppTest page widget state on rerun
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

AppTest keeps `persist_state="page"` widget values, and keyed tab selection, across a same-page rerun, including multipage apps. Each run was building a new page manager that started on an empty page hash, so the script runner treated the rerun as a page change and cleared that state. The new manager now starts on the page hash the previous run finished on, and a rerun that did not call `switch_page()` requests that same hash. `AppTest.switch_page()` still requests the destination page, so a real page change still clears page-scoped values.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #17249

## Testing Plan

- `lib/tests/streamlit/testing/app_test_test.py` — same-page hide/show for `persist_state="page"`, `"session"`, and the default; `switch_page` clears page scope and keeps session scope; keyed tabs stay selected after a child-widget run in a single script, `st.navigation`, and a `pages/` app; a `pages/` app and a widget created before `st.navigation()` keep page scope across a same-page hide/show.

No end-to-end test: a browser session already keeps one page manager, and that path retains the value.

title: Programmatically set selections fail for empty selection
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

The example in https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/data/st.dataframe titled: "Example 2: Programmatically set selections" does not work if we try with empty selections.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
from numpy.random import default_rng as rng

df = pd.DataFrame(rng(0).standard_normal((12, 5)), columns=["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"])

if st.button("Select the first row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [0], "columns": [], "cells": []}}
if st.button("Select no row"):
    st.session_state["data"] = {"selection": {"rows": [], "columns": [], "cells": []}}

event = st.dataframe(
    df,
    key="data",
    on_select="rerun",
    selection_mode=["single-row"],
)

st.code(event.selection)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the code
2. Select a row
3. Click on the button "Select the first row", it works as expected
4. Select a row again
5. Click on the button "Select no row", the dataframe selection state is empty but the table keeps the previous selection.

### Expected Behavior

The row selection should match the dataframe selection state and be empty.

### Current Behavior

The dataframe selection state is empty but the table keeps the previous selection and is not empty.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: WSL Docker
- Browser: Edge

### Additional Information

I remember it worked in Streamlit version 1.57.0 but I am not sure, I may be mistaken.

title: BUG: wrong value returned by backend vs frontend, when a widget is rendered after a previous page run set a default value in session state
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

If a default value is set in session state on one page run, and then subsequently a widget is rendered with a corresponding `key`, then the default value is not picked up properly and the frontend and backend show different values for that widget.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# Sets default on first page run
st.session_state.setdefault("foo", 100.0)

if st.toggle("Show"):
    foo = st.number_input("Foo", key="foo")  # Shows 0.00
    st.write("You entered:", foo)  # Shows 100.0
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1.Turn on the  toggle
2. Compare the value in the widget vs the value printed underneath

### Expected Behavior

The value in the widget should match the number reported underneath.

### Current Behavior

The input widget displays `0.00`, but the backend reports `You entered: 100`.

If `r` is pressed to trigger a re-run, then the frontend updates to display `0.0` and the default value is lost.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: 3.14.7
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

This bug is problematic for more complex pages, where widgets may need to be "loaded" or "reset" programmatically, and some widgets may be conditionally hidden depending on a toggle or checkbox.

The bug does not happen if `persist_state="page"` is passed to `number_input`.

Possibly related: #15660 seems to have fixed a similar bug for when persist_state is passed, but not for when persist_state=None.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #17106: [fix] Delayed keyed widgets adopt stored session state.

related_pr.title: [fix] Delayed keyed widgets adopt stored session state
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Keyed widgets that first render after a prior-run `st.session_state` write now tell the frontend to adopt that stored value, so the UI matches the backend instead of mounting at the widget default.

- Previous-run user keys (for example `setdefault` while the widget is hidden) use the same frontend remount signal as `persist_state` remounts.
- Default unmount for `persist_state=None` is unchanged: hiding a widget that had already registered still resets both sides when no independent user-key entry remains.
- Same delayed-mount pattern as #9082. Unifying widget identity on `key` (#12880) is out of scope: remounts may still allocate a new element id.

Did not change frontend initialization: the existing remount signal is already the targeted path. Did not preserve `persist_state=None` widget-id values on unmount, which would change the #3512 reset.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #17093
- Related #9082

## Testing Plan

title: Dialog crashes on keydown events without a key
description:
### Summary

`st.dialog` with `dismissible=False` attaches a capture-phase document `keydown` listener that calls `e.key.toLowerCase()` without checking that `key` is a string. A synthetic `keydown` with no `key` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toLowerCase')`.

This is the same event class as #17082 (`GlobalHotkeys`), but a separate listener. #17082 / PR #17105 only guards `GlobalHotkeys`. The dialog handler still throws while a non-dismissible dialog is open.

### Minimal reproduction

1. Open a non-dismissible dialog (`st.dialog(..., dismissible=False)`).
2. Dispatch:

```js
document.dispatchEvent(new Event("keydown"))
```

Expected: ignored (there is no key to match as `r`).
Actual: uncaught TypeError from `Dialog.tsx` `handleRKeySuppress`.

### Notes

- The listener is only attached while a non-dismissible dialog is open (`capture=true`).
- Do not `preventDefault` / `stopImmediatePropagation` when there is no string `key` — that would treat the event as an R-key suppress.
- Related: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17082
- Related PR: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17105
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #17111: [fix] Ignore keyless events in dialog R-key handler.

related_pr.title: [fix] Ignore keyless events in dialog R-key handler
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Non-dismissible `st.dialog` now skips capture-phase `keydown` events without a string `key` instead of throwing `TypeError` on `toLowerCase`. Those events are not treated as an R-key suppress (`preventDefault` / `stopImmediatePropagation` are not called).

Chose an early `typeof e.key !== "string"` return to match the `GlobalHotkeys` guard in #17105, rather than coercing with `e.key ?? ""`.

Related: #17082 / https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17105 (GlobalHotkeys only).

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #17107

## Testing Plan

  - `frontend/lib/src/components/elements/Dialog/Dialog.test.tsx` — keyless `keydown` with a non-dismissible dialog open does not throw and does not suppress R

Chose an early `typeof event.key !== "string"` return over coercing with `event.key ?? ""` so non-string keys never enter matching. `Dialog.tsx` still has a related unguarded `e.key.toLowerCase()` — follow-up in #17107.

title: Conditionally created dialog in a fragment stops logically existing after rerun of a fragment while still existing on the website
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

When a fragment gets rerun and it has conditionally rendered child dialog (for example guarded by a button being clicked) the dialog will stop being responsive while still existing on the page

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

@st.dialog("Dialog", dismissible=False)
def show_dialog() -> None:
    if st.button("Increment"):
        st.session_state["clicks"] = st.session_state.get("clicks", 0) + 1
    st.write("Clicks:", st.session_state.get("clicks", 0))

@st.fragment(run_every=5)
def parent_fragment() -> None:
    st.session_state["parent_runs"] = st.session_state.get("parent_runs", 0) + 1
    st.write("Parent runs:", st.session_state["parent_runs"])
    if st.button("Open dialog"):
        show_dialog()

st.write("Open the dialog, then wait for the parent fragment's next automatic rerun (every 5 seconds).")
parent_fragment()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click Open dialog
2. start clicking increment
3. after parent reruns the dialog stops being responsive and streamlit will log The fragment with id <id> does not exist anymore - it might have been removed during a preceding full-app rerun.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog to still be responsive

### Current Behavior

The dialog stops being responsive

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: Python 3.13.13
- Operating System: Linux 7.1.4-arch1-1
- Browser: Firefox

### Additional Information

worked when ran with
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.57.0 streamlit run repro.py
```
stopped working at
```
uv run --no-project --with streamlit==1.58.0 streamlit run repro.py
```
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #17039: [fix] Preserve dialogs across parent fragment reruns.

related_pr.title: [fix] Preserve dialogs across parent fragment reruns
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Dialogs now use a full-app fragment lifetime, keeping their backing callable responsive when the fragment that opened them reruns. Full-app reruns still close dialogs, while ordinary nested fragments retain parent-scoped cleanup.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

Closes #17011.

## Testing Plan

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes fragment storage eviction semantics for dialogs and nested fragments during fragment-only reruns; incorrect lifetime handling could leave stale fragments or break dialog interactivity.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#17011**: when a fragment that opened a dialog reruns alone (`st.rerun` on the parent fragment), the dialog and nested fragments inside it stay interactive instead of being torn down with parent-scoped cleanup.
> 
> The runtime adds **`_FragmentLifetime`** (`PARENT_SCOPED` vs `FULL_APP_SCOPED`) on fragment registration. **`clear_stale_descendants`** now walks the fragment tree and only evicts missing **parent-scoped** children; **full-app-scoped** fragments (and their retained subtrees when the dialog did not re-execute) survive fragment-only reruns but are still dropped on a full app run that does not re-register them.
> 
> **`@st.dialog`** registers its backing `@st.fragment` wrapper with **`FULL_APP_SCOPED`** so the dialog callable outlives the opener fragment’s rerun. Coverage includes new **`MemoryFragmentStorage`** / dialog-decorator unit tests and a Playwright scenario (parent fragment rerun + nested fragment inside the dialog).
>

title: `LinkColumn(width=..., display_text=":material/...` fails to render the icon when the width (in pixels) is less than 4 times the length of the icon's name (in characters)

related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Substitutes the Material Symbols codepoint for `LinkColumn(display_text=":material/open_in_new:")` so the icon still renders in narrow cells. Glide truncates canvas text with `max = cellWidth / 4` before drawing, which slices the `open_in_new` ligature name and leaves truncated icon-name text instead of the glyph.

Other material icons keep the ligature-name path and can still fail in narrow columns. A full icon-name → codepoint map (~15–20kb) and a custom LinkColumn renderer were considered and rejected for this pass. A durable general fix likely belongs in Glide (`truncateString` vs canvas clipping); this repo already patches Glide via `frontend/.yarn/patches` for Streamlit-specific issues, so that is a known follow-up path.

title: Server shutdown fails to exit while processing infinite loop

### Summary

Python process does not exit when shutting down the server while processing an infinite loop in a script

### Steps to reproduce

Unknown

Marks the script-runner thread as a daemon so Ctrl-C / SIGTERM can exit even when a user script is stuck in a loop with no `st.*` interrupt points.

title: `st.metric` docs promise gray for a zero delta but only the literal string `"0"` counts for strings, and the bundled skill's examples are all strings
description: ### Checklist ### Summary This is a documentation inconsistency, not a runtime bug. The behavior is by design (#15790, closing #15005), and this report does not ask to change it. It asks for the two places that describe `delta` to match it. The `delta` docstring gives four unqualified rules ([metric.py lines 150-158](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L150-L158)): no arrow for `None` or an empty string, "if the delta is zero, no arrow is shown and the delta is gray", red and down for "a negative number or starts with a minus sign", otherwise green and up. `delta_color="normal"` repeats "gray when zero" ([metric.py line 170](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L170)) and `delta_arrow="auto"` says "no arrow is shown if `delta` is zero" ([metric.py line 269](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L269)). Those rules treat strings as first-class input (the minus-sign branch exists only for strings), so a reader expects a zero-valued string such as `"0%"` or `"+0.0%"` to be "zero". The implementation defines zero for strings as the literal `"0"` only ([metric.py lines 598-604](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/elements/metric.py#L598-L604)), with the comment "other numeric-looking strings (e.g. `"0.0"`, `"0%"`) stay positive". #15790 added that deliberately, on the basis that string deltas are opaque display text, and locked it in with an anti-regression test. The docstring was not updated to say so, which is the gap. The packaged `developing-with-streamlit` skill widens the gap in practice. Every `st.metric` example in it passes `delta` as a pre-formatted string: [dashboards.md line 17](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/dashboards.md?plain=1#L17), [dashboards.md lines 47-49](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/dashboards.md?plain=1#L47-L49), and [data-display.md line 363](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/2bd9d77e68e1ef6beaee2bcf98da2c0707bacc63/lib/streamlit/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/references/data-display.md?plain=1#L363). The skill never mentions zero, so it does not contradict anything, but an agent that follows its examples and then reads the docstring's "gray when zero" will format a flat period as `"0%"` and get a green up-arrow. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python For reference only. This shows the designed behavior, not a bug; it is here so the mismatch with the docstring wording can be seen without reading the source. import streamlit as st col1, col2, col3 = st.columns(3) # What the skill's examples lead to for a flat period: col1.metric("Orders (skill style)", "1.4k", "0%") # green up-arrow col2.metric("Orders (skill style)", "1.4k", "-0.0%") # red down-arrow # What actually renders neutral: col3.metric("Orders (numeric)", 1400, 0, delta_description="vs last month") "I.e.:" from streamlit.elements.metric import _is_zero_delta for delta in ["0", "0%", "+0.0%", "-0.0%", 0]: repr(delta), _is_zero_delta(delta) # '0' True # '0%' False # '+0.0%' False # '-0.0%' False # 0 True ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Read the `delta` docstring's "if the delta is zero" rule and `delta_color="normal"`'s "gray when zero". 2. `streamlit run` or `uv run streamlit run` the snippet. 3. Compare the first two tiles with the third / see the debug output beneath it. ### Expected Behavior Documentation that states the actual rule: 1. In the `delta` docstring (and the `delta_color` / `delta_arrow` mentions of zero), say that a string delta is displayed as-is and that only the literal string `"0"` is treated as zero; other zero-like strings follow the sign rule (leading minus is negative, anything else is positive). One sentence is enough. 2. In the packaged skill, either show at least one example with a numeric `delta` and qualifier text in `delta_description=`, or add a one-line note next to the string examples that string deltas are never treated as zero. ### Current Behavior The docstring says zero deltas are gray with no qualification about strings. `"0%"` renders as a positive delta with a green up-arrow and `"-0.0%"` as a negative delta with a red down-arrow, which is the designed behavior. The skill's examples are all strings and say nothing about zero. For at-a-glance reference: ### Is this a regression? Not a regression and not a behavior change request. Verified on 1.63.0 and 1.64.0 (the latest release at the time of writing): the docstring text, the skill examples, and `_is_zero_delta` are identical in both, and unchanged at the current tip of `develop`. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.63.0 and 1.64.0, both reproduced - Python version: 3.14.6 - Operating System: Linux Mint 22.3 Zena 64-bit - Browser: Version 152.0.7977.82 (Official Build) for Linux Mint (x86_64) ### Additional Information The behavior was settled in #15790: the PR description lists an anti-regression test that `"0.0"`, `"+0"` and `"0%"` "stay green/up", and review confirmed the numbers-versus-strings split as intended. Nothing here asks to reopen that; it asks for the docstring and the skill to describe it. `format=` is not a way around the string question: it is one format applied to both `value` and `delta`, and `"percent"` multiplies by 100, so a tile whose value is a count and whose delta is a percent change cannot be served by a single `format=`. Numeric `delta` plus `delta_description=` is the pattern that works, and it is the one the skill could show.

title: st.data_editor NumberColumn: typing a value starting with "." (no leading zero) drops the decimal point and reads digits as a whole number
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

When a NumberColumn cell is selected and you type a value that starts with `.` (e.g. `.01`), the `.` is silently dropped and the remaining digits are committed as a whole number — `.01` becomes `1`, `.07` becomes `7`. Typing the same value with a leading zero (`0.01`) works correctly, and **pasting** `.01` into the cell also works correctly. So this is specific to the character-by-character typed-entry path.

Impact
This is a real-world data-entry trap: any user in the habit of typing .01-style shorthand (common for percentage/margin fields) silently enters a value the cell just shows a plausible-looking wrong number.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st
df = pd.DataFrame({"Customer": ["A", "B"], "Margin": [12.0, 8.0]})
st.data_editor(
    df,
    column_config={
        "Margin": st.column_config.NumberColumn("Margin", format="%.4f", step=0.0001),
    },
)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Click the Margin cell for row A (shows 12.0000).
Type .07 (as literal keystrokes: ., 0, 7).
Press Enter.

### Expected Behavior

Expected: cell shows 0.0700.

### Current Behavior

Actual: cell shows 7.0000.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

Streamlit version: 1.61.1
Python version: 3.12/3.14
Browser: Chrome
OS: Windows

### Additional Information

_No response_

title: Scroll to st.chat_input
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

Placing `st.chat_input` inside `st.bottom` causes an otherwise non-chat page to scroll to the bottom immediately on initial load, without any user interaction or chat messages. This hides the heading and initial content when using the bottom container for a persistent assistant alongside a dashboard. Replacing only `st.chat_input` with `st.text_input` prevents the unsolicited scrolling.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.title("Dashboard heading")
for number in range(30):
    st.write(f"Dashboard row {number}")

with st.bottom:
    st.chat_input("Ask about the dashboard")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install `streamlit==1.63.0` and run the example with `streamlit run app.py`.
2. Open a fresh browser tab/context with a viewport around 1280 x 720, so the main content exceeds the viewport height.
3. Do not click, type, or scroll. Wait for rendering to settle.
4. Observe that the main page has scrolled to the bottom and the dashboard heading is offscreen.
5. As a control, replace `st.chat_input` with `st.text_input`, restart/reload in a fresh browser context, and observe that the page stays at the top.

No custom CSS, JavaScript, Snowflake connection, fragments, tabs, navigation, or third-party component is needed to reproduce this.

### Expected Behavior

An initial dashboard load should remain at the top. A bottom-docked input should not make non-chat content above it auto-scroll before any conversation exists. If automatic scrolling is intentional for chat-first apps, an opt-out for this mixed dashboard/assistant use case would be helpful.

### Current Behavior

The page scrolls to the bottom on its own. In three fresh Chrome contexts per variant, measured after rendering settled at a 1280 x 720 viewport:

| Bottom widget | Main scrollTop | Main scrollHeight | Main clientHeight |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `st.chat_input` (all 3 runs) | 843 | 1563 | 720 |
| `st.text_input` (all 3 control runs) | 0 | 1573 | 720 |

The scroll position was read from the main scrollable section (`section.stMain`), not `window.scrollY`. No Streamlit exception was displayed. Measurements used Playwright with installed Chrome in headless mode; the same symptom was first noticed in interactive Chrome in a larger app.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.63.0 (also the latest GitHub release at the time of filing)
- Python version: 3.14.3
- Operating System: macOS 26.6, ARM64
- Browser: Google Chrome 152.0.7977.83
- Deployment: local `streamlit run`, default theme for the minimal example

### Additional Information

_No response_

title: Back button changes URL query params but not `st.query_params` until user leaves page and comes back
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

When using `st.query_params` to modify the current URL, new items are added to the browser history so one can navigate forwards and backwards to the URLs that have previously been set.

- On using the forwards and backwards buttons in the browser, the URL changes as expected, but calls to `st.query_params` see only the final version of the URL.
    - This only happens if `st.navigation` is used - if the app is single-page, the forwards and backwards buttons don't trigger a rerun of the back end at all (as in #13853). 
- If the user navigates to a different page, the forwards and backwards buttons DO cause the `st.query_params` to change.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import datetime

import streamlit as st

def page():
    st.write(datetime.datetime.now())

    if st.button("Increment Query Param"):
        value = int(st.query_params.get("value", "0"))
        st.query_params["value"] = value + 1

    st.write(st.query_params)

st.navigation([
    st.Page(page, title="Query Params", default=True),
    st.Page(lambda: None, title="Other Page", url_path="other"),
]).run()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the app URL in a browser
2. Press the "Increment Query Param" button twice - the URL should now end `?value=2`
3. Press the browser's back button
4. Press the browser's forwards button
5. Click on "Other Page" in the nav bar
6. Press the browser's back button
7. Press the browser's back button again

### Expected Behavior

1. The URL has no query parameters and the printed `st.query_params` are empty
2. The URL ends with `?value=2` and the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "2"`
3. The URL ends with `?value=1` and the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "1"`
4. The URL ends with `?value=2` and the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "2"`
5. The URL has no query parameters, no content is shown
6. The URL ends with `?value=2` and the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "2"`
7. The URL ends with `?value=1` and the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "1"`

### Current Behavior

After step 3: the printed `st.query_params` shows `"value": "2"` (the timestamp and URL do update, but the `st.query_params` appear to be cached)

Notes:
- after steps 5 and 6 (navigate to a different page and back), step 7 (apparently identical to step 3) works as expected
- replacing step 5 with "navigate to an external site" also makes step 7 work, albeit now in a new session

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `1.54.0`
- Python version: `3.11.11`, `3.13.1`
- Operating System: `Windows 11`
- Browser: `Edge 145.0`, `Chrome 145.0`, `Firefox 147.0`

### Additional Information

_No response_

related_pr.title: [fix] Sync st.query_params on same-page browser back/forward
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

When browser back/forward changes only the query string on the same multipage
app page, `st.query_params` now follows the restored URL, and later widget
reruns stay aligned with the address bar (including embed hosts).

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

Closes #13963

Co-authored-by: Harshang Akabari <a.harshang@gmail.com>

## Testing Plan




---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches browser history, rerun query-string plumbing, and embed host messaging—behavioral changes in navigation edge cases, but scoped with targeted unit and E2E tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`st.query_params` staying stale** when browser back/forward only changes the query string on the **same multipage route** (closes #13963).
> 
> The frontend now treats the **URL as source of truth** on `popstate`: it normalizes query strings via a shared **`normalizeQueryString`** helper (strips a leading `?` everywhere query strings are compared or merged), updates app/host state with **`syncQueryParams`**, and passes the live query string into **`onPageChange`** so reruns use the restored bar value instead of cached React state. Anchor-only same-page navigation still skips reruns when the query string is unchanged; embed **`UPDATE_FROM_QUERY_PARAMS`** reruns with the normalized override without echoing **`SET_QUERY_PARAM`**.
>

title: Unsafe `shell=True` grep interpolates snapshot filenames in `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py`
description:
**Description**

`scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` builds a `grep` command by interpolating snapshot
filenames from the working tree into a shell string that is then executed with
`shell=True`, so shell metacharacters in committed snapshot filenames execute
arbitrary commands when the script is run.

In `scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` (lines 225-228):

```python
cmd = f'grep -r --include="*.py" "{snapshot_name}" e2e_playwright/'
result = subprocess.run(
    cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
)
```

The `snapshot_name` is derived from on-disk filenames (lines 288-311):

```python
for dirpath, _, filenames in os.walk(snapshot_root):  # e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux
    for filename in filenames:
        if filename.endswith(".png"):
            all_snapshot_files.append(os.path.join(dirpath, filename))
...
snapshot_name = re.sub(r"\[.*\]\.png$", "", filename)
```

`filename` comes straight from the repository working tree (the snapshot PNGs
are committed to git), so anyone whose snapshot file gets merged controls part
of the command string. Because the value is placed inside double quotes,
`/bin/sh` still interprets `"`, `;`, `|`, `$()` and backticks — for example a
file named `st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "[chromium].png` is reduced to the
snapshot name `st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "` and produces

    grep -r --include="*.py" "st_button"; touch /tmp/pwned; "" e2e_playwright/

which runs `touch /tmp/pwned` as a separate command. The remaining grep then
searches for the same injected string, keeping the script's normal flow intact.

**Trigger scenario**

1. A PR adds (or renames) a snapshot file under
   `e2e_playwright/__snapshots__/linux/` with a filename containing shell
   metacharacters (the name is visible in the diff, but its effect is easy to
   miss in review).
2. The PR is merged.
3. A maintainer runs `python scripts/snapshot_cleanup.py` locally, or CI runs
   it in `--ci` mode — both paths execute the grep above.
4. The injected command executes in the maintainer's environment / CI runner.

**Impact**

Arbitrary command execution in the environment of whoever runs the cleanup
script. In practice the attacker already needs write access to the repository
(a merged PR), so I'd class this as a hardening issue rather than a security
vulnerability — which is why I'm opening a regular issue instead of using a
security channel. Still, it's an easy footgun to eliminate: the `find` call a
few lines above (lines 157-160) also uses `shell=True` (its string is static,
so it is harmless, but it could be cleaned up in the same pass).

**Suggested fix**

Drop the shell entirely and pass an argument list, keeping `--` to avoid
option injection:

```python
result = subprocess.run(
    ["grep", "-r", "--include=*.py", "--", snapshot_name, "e2e_playwright/"],
    capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,
)
```

Optionally validate the name as defense in depth, e.g.
`re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.\-]+", snapshot_name)` (or use `shlex.quote()` if a
shell must be kept).

I'd be happy to open a PR switching both `shell=True` call sites to the
argument-list form if that's welcome. Thanks for maintaining a great project!

title: st.slider corrupts min_value/max_value when bounds are reversed, silently producing a wrong range
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

`_slider()` tries to swap reversed bounds with two sequential statements, but the second one reads the variable the first one just overwrote:

```python
# lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/slider.py:1081-1083
# Ensure that min <= value(s) <= max, adjusting the bounds as necessary.
min_value = min(min_value, max_value)
max_value = max(min_value, max_value)   # <-- min_value is already the new (smaller) value
```

After line 1082, `min_value` is `min(a, b)`, so line 1083 evaluates `max(min(a, b), b)`, which is always `b`. The original `min_value` can never become the upper bound, so the intended swap never happens. Depending on what `value` is, this silently produces a wrong range or raises an exception quoting numbers the user never passed.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

# 1. Bounds silently reinterpreted
st.slider("a", 10, 1)                                  # -> range 1..10, value 10

# 2. Upper bound silently invented from `value`
st.slider("b", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=5)     # -> range 1..5  (max_value=1 is gone)

# 3. Spurious exception quoting numbers the user never passed
st.slider("c", min_value=10, max_value=1, value=1)     # -> StreamlitAPIException
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run any of the three lines above.
2. Compare the resulting slider bounds against the arguments passed.

### Expected Behavior

Either of the following would be self-consistent:

- Reject reversed bounds with a clear error naming the two values the caller actually supplied, the way `st.date_input` already does:
  > The `min_value`, set to 2024-01-02, shouldn't be larger than the `max_value`, set to 2024-01-01.
- Or genuinely swap them, so `st.slider("a", 10, 1)` yields a `1..10` slider — which is what the code comment says it intends.

Today it does neither reliably.

### Current Behavior

Verified with `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest`:

```
slider(min=10, max=1)            -> min=1.0 max=10.0 value=10
slider(min=10, max=1, value=5)   -> min=1.0 max=5.0  value=5
slider(min=10, max=1, value=1)   -> RAISED: Slider `min_value` must be less than the `max_value`.
                                            The values were 1 and 1.
```

Note case 3: the user passed `10` and `1`, but the error reports "The values were 1 and 1" — both numbers have been overwritten by the faulty normalization. Case 2 is the most damaging, because it silently produces a slider whose upper bound (`5`) was never supplied as a bound at all; it leaked in from `value`.

Isolating just the two lines:

```python
min_value, max_value = 10, 1
min_value = min(min_value, max_value)
max_value = max(min_value, max_value)
print(min_value, max_value)   # 1 1     <-- current behavior

min_value, max_value = 10, 1
min_value, max_value = min(min_value, max_value), max(min_value, max_value)
print(min_value, max_value)   # 1 10    <-- intended
```

The `min_value == max_value` guard at line 1137 then fires on values that are an artifact of this bug rather than of user input, and it only catches the case where the corruption happens to collapse both bounds to the same number — which is why `st.slider("x", 5, 5)` errors while `st.slider("x", 10, 1)` does not.

### Suggested Fix

Assign both bounds simultaneously (or compute the max from the original value):

```python
min_value, max_value = min(min_value, max_value), max(min_value, max_value)
```

### Acceptance Criteria

### Is this a regression?

Unknown.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`, commit `2ac0d77d3`)
- Python version: 3.13.6
- Operating System: Windows 11 (logic is platform-independent)
- Browser: n/a (reproduced headlessly via `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest`)

### Additional Information

Related but distinct: #5099 covers `value` falling outside `(min_value, max_value)`. This report is specifically about the bound-normalization statements corrupting `min_value`/`max_value` themselves.

title: Stale output from a long-running computation erroneously shows as not stale when app rerun
description:
### Checklist


### Summary

This is a bug report on behalf of Thiago in order to keep it tracked.

When a Streamlit app with long-running computation is stopped and then re-run, old stale data from the previous run show up as if it was not stale until the old thread completes execution, at which point the data is properly cleaned up.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import platform
import time

import streamlit as st

st.caption(
    f"""
Running with Python {platform.python_version()} and Streamlit {st.__version__}.
"""
)

"""
This is an app!!
"""


def slow_computation(x):
    st.write("Starting slow computation...")
    time.sleep(10)
    st.write("Stopping slow computation...")
    return f"Done, {x + 1}"


out = slow_computation(1)

st.write(out)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

This is a Playwright test that simulates the current behavior (which is to say, this test currently passes, but should fail once the underlying issue is fixed). There are `NOTE`s inline that describe expected behavior


```py
import time

from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect


def test_threading_behavior(page: Page):
    # This uses `localhost:8501` since I was running different versions of Streamlit
    # in an attempt to bisect this issue in case it was introduced at some point in time
    page.goto("http://localhost:8501/")

    page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...").wait_for(timeout=20000)
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).to_be_visible()

    print(page.query_selector_all(".element-container")[0].inner_text())

    # At this point, the first run of the thread completed
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).to_be_visible()

    # conditional logic to make it work with older versions of Streamlit
    if page.query_selector('div[data-testid="stMainMenu"]'):
        page.get_by_test_id("stMainMenu").click()
    elif page.query_selector('[id="MainMenu"]'):
        main_menu = page.query_selector('[id="MainMenu"]')
        if main_menu:
            main_menu.click()

    # Now we are re-running the app
    page.get_by_text("Rerun").click()

    # Some time delay so that the new thread is started and some elements are marked as stable
    time.sleep(2)

    # Expect some of the elements to be marked as stale
    assert len(page.query_selector_all('div[data-stale="true"]')) == 2
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).to_be_visible()
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).to_be_visible()

    # Stop the new thread
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Stop").click()

    time.sleep(2)

    # NOTE: This should not pass. Stale elements shouldn't suddenly be marked as not stale
    # since these are old results from a thread that was supposed to have been stopped
    assert len(page.query_selector_all('div[data-stale="true"]')) == 0

    # NOTE: This should not pass. It is unexpected that the results from the old thread
    # are still showing up, despite us re-running
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).to_be_visible()
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).to_be_visible()

    # wait for the thread to complete
    time.sleep(10)

    # Expect old elements to be cleared out
    expect(page.get_by_text("Stopping slow computation...")).not_to_be_visible()
    expect(page.get_by_text("Done, 2")).not_to_be_visible()
```

### Expected Behavior

_No response_

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?


### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.0.0 -> 1.40.1 all show this behavior (I didn't test versions before)
- Python version: 3.8
- Operating System: Mac
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16839: [fix] Keep elements stale while a stop is pending.

related_pr.title: [fix] Keep elements stale while a stop is pending
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Pressing Stop no longer un-dims leftover elements from earlier script runs. A pending stop does not end
execution, so `isElementStale` now treats `STOP_REQUESTED` like `RUNNING` until the run actually
finishes — previously those elements reported `data-stale="false"` the instant Stop was pressed.

That window is often long rather than momentary: execution control is only checked when a ForwardMsg
is enqueued, so a script blocked in a non-interruptible call keeps running until its next `st.*` call.
Stopping a 10-minute query un-dimmed the whole page for 10 minutes.

Two consequences beyond dimming, both improvements:

- `balloons` / `snow` no longer remount and replay their animation mid-stop (`hideIfStale` unmounts
  rather than dims, so un-staling them re-triggered the effect).
- A leftover tab stays disabled instead of becoming clickable moments before `clearStaleNodes` deletes it.

The fix was originally identified in #13787; that contributor is credited as co-author. Note that
PR's backend half — routing user stops to `FINISHED_EARLY_FOR_RERUN` — is **not** included here and
would be a regression: it makes the frontend skip `clearStaleNodes`, leaving stale elements dimmed
indefinitely. The e2e test below guards against that, which unit tests cannot.

Scoped deliberately to `isElementStale`. `shouldComponentBeEnabled`, a few lines above, still
special-cases only `RUNNING`, so an `empty` placeholder becomes enabled the moment Stop is pressed.
That inconsistency is real but has no visible effect (empty containers render nothing), and widening
it would unfreeze `Maybe`-gated placeholder updates during the stop window — a behavior change
outside a staleness fix. Left for its own change.

Scope note on the linked issue: it carries two expectations. The first — that leftovers must not flip to
non-stale when Stop is pressed — is what this fixes. The second, that the previous run's output should not
still be on screen at all, is inherent rather than a defect: a script blocked in a non-interruptible call
cannot be preempted, so its elements can only be cleared once it actually reaches a checkpoint. The
issue's own closing assertions cover that, and they already pass — leftovers are removed when the stopped
run finishes.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

Closes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9904

## Testing Plan

- **Unit Tests (JS):** `STOP_REQUESTED` cases mirroring the existing `RUNNING` pair, including the
  fragment path. The pre-existing "returns false for all other script run states" case had
  `STOP_REQUESTED` removed from its array — it asserted the bug verbatim; the remaining entries still
  guard the fallthrough.
- **E2E Tests:** `appnode_hierarchy_test.py` asserts leftovers stay stale through the stop window and
  are cleared once the run finishes. Verified it fails without the production change
  (`data-stale="false"` on 12 containers), and 5 consecutive runs pass.
- Run locally on macOS/chromium; no snapshots involved, so nothing to regenerate.

---

Co-Authored-By: Harshang Akabari <a.harshang@gmail.com>

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core render-tree staleness during script execution, but the change is narrowly scoped to treating STOP_REQUESTED like RUNNING in isElementStale, with unit and e2e regression coverage.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a regression where pressing **Stop** immediately cleared `data-stale` on leftover UI from earlier runs, even though the script was still executing until the next checkpoint.
> 
> **`isElementStale`** now applies the same fragment/script-run-id rules for **`STOP_REQUESTED`** as for **`RUNNING`**, so dimmed leftovers stay stale through the pending-stop window and related behaviors (e.g. balloons/snow remounting, tabs briefly re-enabling) no longer flip mid-stop. **`shouldComponentBeEnabled`** is unchanged and still only special-cases **`RUNNING`**.
> 
> Unit tests parameterize the existing running staleness cases over both states and add coverage when **`fragmentIdsThisRun`** is omitted. A new Playwright test on the long-compute scenario asserts stale leftovers persist while **`stopRequested`**, then disappear after the run finishes (guarding against routing user stops in a way that skips **`clearStaleNodes`**).
>

related_pr.title: [fix] Stringify list columns PyArrow cannot serialize
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Stringify mixed list-like columns that PyArrow cannot serialize, instead of crashing `st.dataframe` /
`st.data_editor` when nesting levels differ.

`determine_arrow_column_fix` judged a mixed-dtype object column from its first non-null value alone, so
columns mixing list nesting levels — `[1, 2]` next to `[[1, 2], [3, 4]]`, or a GeoJSON Polygon next to a
MultiPolygon — were judged Arrow-compatible and then raised during serialization. The existing dict and
frozenset gates are unchanged; a trial `pa.array()` conversion is now the final gate of that branch.

- The trial conversion is **additive on purpose**. Dict columns *pass* `pa.array` but must still be
  stringified for Arrow JS, and frozensets/ExtensionArrays *raise* but want the list fix. Replacing the
  single-value checks with the probe would regress both.
- `st.data_editor` previously crashed with a raw `pyarrow.lib.ArrowInvalid` — no Streamlit error at all.
  It now stringifies and disables the column, and raises `StreamlitDataframeConversionError` if
  serialization still fails, matching `st.dataframe`.
- `trial_conversion=False` keeps the expensive gate off `st.data_editor`'s per-rerun path, which calls
  this for every column. It runs only after a serialization failure. On a 200k × 4 frame including a
  list column: **46.9 ms before, 47.0 ms after** (68.7 ms without the opt-out).

The `except` around the probe is deliberately broad. `pa.array` can raise outside PyArrow's own error
types — `pd.Series([[2**70], [1]])` raises `OverflowError` — and the function's contract is to return a
verdict, not to raise. The `try` body is a single call, so there is no application logic for a broad
catch to mask.

`built_in_chart_utils` skips the trial probe because that preprocessing runs on every chart render. The
melted scalar y column can never reach it — the gate requires `infer_dtype` to return exactly `"mixed"`,
and melting scalars yields `"mixed-integer"` or `"floating"` — but the unmelted `columns_to_leave_alone`
id columns (`x`, `size`, `sort`) can, and did. Incompatible values are still handled by the subsequent
Arrow serialization retry. Verified to leave the Vega spec and Arrow payload byte-identical, while
reducing a 400k-row melt from **56.2 ms to 11.3 ms** per render.

**Also fixes a MultiIndex bug this PR surfaced.** `st.data_editor`'s pre-emptive pass ran before
`_fix_column_headers`, so for MultiIndex columns it registered `disabled` under `"('a', 'b')"` rather
than the flattened `"a_b"` — a stringified but still *editable* column. The retry path added here keys
correctly, so the two disagreed. The pass now runs after the flatten. Note this affects MultiIndex
editors with **any** Arrow-incompatible column, not only the nested-list shapes above.

Two gaps left deliberately, both pre-existing in kind: a frozenset next to a nested list still raises for
`st.dataframe` (the frozenset gate returns `"list"` before the probe, and nothing re-checks after the
conversion), and a mixed `pd.Index` is stringified by an earlier defensive branch so the probe never
sees it.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

Closes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9380

## Testing Plan

- **Unit Tests (Python):** the failing shapes in both orders, with a leading null and the GeoJSON case;
  the non-triggering shapes (consistent nesting, tuples, ragged lists, `list + None`) so the probe can't
  over-fire; the `OverflowError` shape; the `disabled` config reaching a column fixed via the retry; and
  the new `StreamlitDataframeConversionError` path.
- **No E2E:** stringified-incompatible-column is already covered end-to-end by `UNSUPPORTED_TYPES_DF`
  (which carries `period`, `complex` and dict columns). This adds a new *input* shape to an
  already-covered *output* path.
- **Manual:** rendered in a browser against a production build — both `st.dataframe` and `st.data_editor`,
  with a consistently-nested control column confirmed still rendering as a list. The GeoJSON values are
  fully legible at default column width, which was the reporter's actual ask. A pre-fix build was used as
  a control to confirm the crash.

---

**Contribution License Agreement**

By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core Arrow serialization and per-rerun data-editor/chart preprocessing; behavior is mostly additive (stringify/disable) but affects performance and which columns stay editable.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes crashes when **object columns mix list nesting levels** (e.g. `[1, 2]` beside `[[1, 2], [3, 4]]`, GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon) that PyArrow rejects but the old “first non-null value” heuristic treated as safe.
> 
> **Arrow compatibility detection** adds an optional **`pa.array()` trial** (with **`OverflowError`** in the shared conversion-error set) and a **`trial_conversion`** flag so hot paths can skip the probe. **`st.data_editor`** now stringifies and **disables** bad columns (after header flattening), **retries** Arrow conversion on failure, and raises **`StreamlitDataframeConversionError`** instead of a raw PyArrow error; **built-in charts** pass **`trial_conversion=False`** and rely on the existing serialize-and-retry path for speed.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit afb17d77a4fd5ea6128dcdd9e092fc39d3d413dd. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: `setTriggerValue` called during mount is dropped ~1 in 4 times when the component remounts, despite an explicit `key`
description:
### Summary

When a Components V2 component calls `setTriggerValue` during mount (inside the default function, rather than from a user event handler), values are silently lost if the component remounts because its `data` changed — even when an explicit `key` is passed, which keeps the element id stable.

Measured roughly a quarter loss: **5 of 21 values sent were never received by Python at all.** They are not late — a scan of the entire session log shows they never arrive in any subsequent run.

This is split out of #14710, where it surfaced during investigation. It is distinct from the two by-design mechanisms discussed there (`data` participating in element identity for unkeyed components, and trigger values resetting after each run).

**Update — measured root cause.** A frontend race in `WidgetStateManager.removeInactive`: it destroys the synthetic trigger-aggregator widget state while that state is still awaiting its batched flush, so the app reruns with no trigger at all. Not a backend discard. Measured on a production build with the repro below: 10/85 values lost unpatched vs 0/85 patched, and with instrumentation, 14/14 losses correlated exactly with the destroying call. Mechanism and open question under Additional Information.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

comp = st.components.v2.component(
    "repro.mount_trigger",
    js="""
    export default function (component) {
        const v = "val" + component.data.nonce;
        console.log("SEND " + v);
        component.setTriggerValue("v", v);
    }
    """,
)

if "clicks" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.clicks = 0
if st.button("bump"):
    st.session_state.clicks += 1

nonce = f"c{st.session_state.clicks}"
result = comp(data={"nonce": nonce}, key="stable_key")

received = result.get("v")
st.write(f"data nonce {nonce} -> received {received!r}")
print(f"nonce={nonce} received={received!r}", flush=True)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and open the browser console.
2. Click **bump** ~20 times, letting the app settle between clicks. Each click changes `data`, so the component remounts and sends one value.
3. Compare the `SEND val…` lines in the console against the `received=…` lines in the terminal.
4. Roughly one in four sent values never appears on the Python side.

### Expected Behavior

Every value the mounted component sends is readable on the following script run. The explicit `key` makes the element id stable, so a changing `data` payload should not affect delivery.

### Current Behavior

About 25% of values are never delivered. Verified as lost rather than late by scanning the full backend log after all clicks — 0 arrived in a later run.

The element id was logged each run and confirmed identical throughout (`$$ID-b4c118c7288cf7d656c205e58a384db6-stable_key`), so this is not the identity churn that affects unkeyed components.

Three controls on the same harness came out clean. They do not isolate the bug to trigger-on-mount — see Additional Information — but they do narrow which write path is affected:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| `setStateValue` on mount, same conditions | 21/21 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, stable `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| `setTriggerValue` from a user event handler, churning `data` | 20/20 delivered |
| **`setTriggerValue` on mount, churning `data`** | **5 of 21 lost** |

### Additional Information

**Mechanism.** `setTriggerValue` writes to a synthetic aggregator widget id (`makeTriggerAggregatorId` → `$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<componentId>__events`) and the flush is deferred to a `setTimeout(…, 0)` macrotask. `App.removeInactiveWidgetState()` runs from the `ScriptFinished` → `clearStaleNodes` setState callback and deletes every widget state whose id is not an active *element* id — the aggregator id never is, because it isn't part of the element tree. When that lands before the flush, the trigger is deleted but the rerun is still sent (`sendUpdateWidgetsMessage` uses unfiltered `createWidgetStatesMsg()`), so the script reruns with no trigger.

Mount-time triggers are the most exposed path: the component's `default function` runs behind `await loadAndRunModule(...)` (dynamic `import()` of a blob URL), so it executes a macrotask or more after the commit that mounted it. This also explains the control table — `setStateValue` is immune because it writes the component's real element id, and the event-handler controls passed because letting the app settle means `removeInactive` has already run.

**The `_pending_resets` theory is ruled out.** It is only populated by `mark_page_switch_drops`, which runs on page transitions and skips widgets whose recorded page is the current page, so a single-page app never populates it. (For the record, the original hypothesis was that `_pending_resets` in `lib/streamlit/runtime/state/session_state.py` discarded a frontend-resent value on re-registration, which would have made this by design.)

**Related blind spot.** The same synthetic id is invisible to other active-id filters, not just this one: `App.tsx` `onPageChange` sends `getActiveWidgetStates(activeWidgetIds)`, which would likewise drop a pending aggregator. Reaching it would require a trigger and a page navigation in the same macrotask, and dropping a trigger while navigating away is defensible, so no change is planned there. Recorded as an observation only.

**Scope of what was tested.** Measured against this repro on one machine, 235 trials total. It establishes this race as the cause of the loss seen here; it does not rule out other trigger-loss paths. The same race also appears to explain the recurring `bidi_components/basics_test.py::test_trigger_interactions` CI flake — the failure signature (counts unchanged plus `Result` reset to `None`) is what a trigger-less rerun produces — but that link is inferred from the signature, not directly observed. Two prior automated PRs (#14542, #14843) misattributed that flake to a slow iframe round-trip and raised timeouts.

**Open question for Components V2** (replacing the original question here, which is now answered — the drop is a race, not intentional): should `setTriggerValue` during mount be a supported pattern at all? Fixing the race makes it reliable, but it fires on every remount, so churning `data` produces one trigger per remount. That is a semantics decision independent of this bug, and it determines whether this issue closes as fixed or splits into a fix plus a documentation/warning change.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (released wheel, production frontend build)
- Python version: 3.11 · macOS · Chromium
- The ~25% figure is one 21-trial sample on a single machine; treat it as "roughly a quarter" rather than a precise rate.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16833: [fix] Stop dropping in-flight Custom Components v2 triggers.

related_pr.title: [fix] Stop dropping in-flight Custom Components v2 triggers
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Retain in-flight trigger widget state in `removeInactive`, so a Custom Components v2 aggregator written before its batched `setTimeout(0)` flush isn't deleted as stale. The callback then fires and the value reaches Python instead of the script rerunning with no trigger.

`setTriggerValue` writes to a synthetic aggregator widget id (`$$STREAMLIT_INTERNAL_KEY_<componentId>__events`), and `removeInactive` deletes every widget state whose id isn't an active *element* id — which that synthetic id never is. The window is reachable because deltas and `ScriptFinished` arrive as separate WebSocket frames with separate React commits, so `removeInactive` can fire a macrotask or more after the DOM already shows the new output. Mount-time triggers are the most exposed path, since the component's `default function` runs behind a dynamic `import()`.

The fix retains `pendingTriggerIds` for widget states and form widget states. Element states keep following `activeIds`, since they never enter the rerun message.

Measured on a production build against the repro in the issue: **10 of 85 values lost before, 0 of 85 after**. An instrumented build showed 14 losses correlating exactly with 14 destroying calls across 150 further trials.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Fixes #16732. Deliberately not an auto-closing reference: that issue also carries an open question about whether mount-time `setTriggerValue` should be a supported pattern, which this doesn't answer.

## Testing Plan


Three tests in `WidgetStateManager.test.ts`. Two fail without the fix: in-flight retention (plus a stale widget asserted removed, so it can't pass with `removeInactive` as a no-op), and the form-scoped branch. The third — a trigger id dropped after its flush has run — passes either way by design; it guards the retention semantics and fails if `pendingTriggerIds.clear()` is removed.

No new E2E test: reproducing the race in a browser needs artificial delays on both the flush and `removeInactive`, which don't belong in the suite.

`basics_test.py` also had eight assertions that asserted nothing — `expect(locator)` with no `.to_be_visible()` — five of them inside `test_trigger_interactions`. All eight are now real and pass, and the two that are string prefixes of a longer state dict now use `exact=True`.

**Flaky-test verification: [100 iterations, all green](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/actions/runs/33954366950).** That is 300 executions of `test_trigger_interactions` across chromium, firefox and webkit with `--reruns 0`, so nothing was retried away. Per `scripts/fetch_flaky_tests.py`, this test recorded 8 reruns over the previous 14 days — the most flaky test in the repo, on all three browsers — so 300 executions is roughly half the CI exposure that produced them. At that ~1.3% per-execution rate, the chance of seeing zero failures if the flake were still present is ~2%; even at half that rate it is ~13%. `st_form_test.py` also passes 27/27, since the fix touches form widget states.

## Notes for reviewers

- **On the recurring `test_trigger_interactions` flake.** Two automated PRs (#14542, #14843) attributed it to a slow iframe round-trip and raised timeouts. That diagnosis was wrong: a slow round-trip leaves the previous step's `Result` intact, whereas the CI failures show `Result` reset to `None`, which only a trigger-less rerun produces. With the race artificially amplified the test fails with exactly that signature and passes with this fix. This therefore removes the `timeout=10000` #14843 added for the misdiagnosed cause, so a regression fails in ~5s instead of being masked for 10; the 100-iteration run above covers that change at the default timeout. The initial-load timeout stays, since iframe first paint genuinely can lag.
- Retention is bounded to one macrotask: every writer that adds to `pendingTriggerIds` calls `scheduleFlush` synchronously, and that flush deletes the state and clears the set. `removeInactive` is on the rerun hot path, so it short-circuits to `activeIds` when nothing is in flight — the common case allocates nothing.
- At the state-machine level, a form-scoped trigger followed by synchronous submission can double-send through the pre-existing queued flush, and in one narrow ordering this fix reaches that instead of silently losing the trigger. No current product path produces that ordering — every `submitForm` call site is a submit click or Enter keypress, and none writes a trigger in the same handler — and CCv2 ignores triggers inside forms. Traced in the review threads rather than filed as an issue.
- `onPageChange` sends `getActiveWidgetStates(activeWidgetIds)`, which has the same synthetic-id gap. Reaching it needs a trigger and a page navigation in the same macrotask, and dropping a trigger while navigating away is defensible — noted, not changed.
- #16732 carries an open question this doesn't answer: should `setTriggerValue` during mount be a supported pattern? It fires on every remount, so churning `data` produces one trigger per remount. That's a Components V2 semantics decision, and it determines whether the issue closes here or splits off a docs/warning change.

title: (CommunityCloud) Moving slider seems to generate 2 new (empty) window.history states
description:
### Checklist


### Summary

While investigating https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-9184 I noticed my browser history (i.e. back navigation) got _filled_ with `window.history` state entries that don't actually seem to do anything when you navigate backwards or forwards through them. It seems like this only affects community cloud? I was unable to reproduce on a local instance of streamlit.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
st.slider("Slider (1.0 float step)", min_value=1.50, max_value=100.50, value=(2.5, 41.5), step=1.0)
st.slider("Slider (1.1 float step)", min_value=1.50, max_value=100.50, value=(2.5, 41.5), step=1.1)
st.slider("Slider (int step)", min_value=1, max_value=100, value=(2, 40), step=3)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-9184 in MS Edge or Opera One(version: 114.0.5282.185) -- it probably works in Chrome too but I didn't have that installed to test.
2. Right click on the browser "Back" button to see the tab history. It should look something like this
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6154ef06-c882-4c98-ad93-b340fb92a935)

4. Go back and right-click on the browser "Back" button.

5. Clicking the "Back" button doesn't actually change any kind of state on the page (e.g. it doesn't move the sliders back to their old positions -- not that I was really expecting it to do that)



### Expected Behavior

We shouldn't be putting do-nothing states into user's `window.history` on widget interaction.

### Current Behavior

![image](https://external-content.duckduckgo.com/iu/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fi.imgflip.com%2F1rpt5c.jpg&f=1&nofb=1&ipt=53ccae2a973a336828bfcaf6c76821c6c0278814b51b2fd6bdaca1150f84b1ce&ipo=images)

### Is this a regression?


### Debug info

- Streamlit version: whatever you guys were running on Community Cloud in Nov 2024

- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Tested on MS Edge Version 131.0.2903.51 and Opera One (version: 114.0.5282.185)


### Additional Information

## Describe your changes

Apps that assign `st.query_params` on every run added a browser history entry per rerun, so the Back button only stepped through duplicate URLs instead of leaving the app. `history.pushState` creates an entry even when the URL is unchanged, so `App.handlePageInfoChanged` now skips it when the query string already matches `document.location.search`.

title: st.download_button: a filename containing a double quote produces a malformed Content-Disposition header
description:
### Summary

The media endpoint that serves `st.download_button` files builds its `Content-Disposition` header by interpolating the download filename into a quoted string, `filename="{filename}"`, whenever the name is latin-1 encodable. A double quote is latin-1 encodable, so any filename containing one closes the quoted parameter early and the rest of the name spills out as trailing tokens. The emitted header is not valid per RFC 6266, and the name the browser saves the file under is no longer the name the app set.

This needs nothing adversarial to hit. An ordinary filename like `5" x 7" print.jpg` (inch marks) is enough. The name reaches this sink from `st.download_button(file_name=...)`, and since 1.61.0 also from the filename inferred off an uploaded file when `file_name` is omitted.

The safe branch already exists in the same function: a name that is not latin-1 encodable takes `filename*=utf-8''{quote(filename)}`, which percent-encodes and cannot break out. The bug is only which branch a name reaches. Streamlit's own dependency, Starlette, makes the correct choice for the same header in `FileResponse` (`starlette/responses.py`), selecting the quoted form only when `quote(filename) == filename`.

### Reproducible Code Example

Fully in-process against the real media route, no browser needed:

```python
from starlette.applications import Starlette
from starlette.testclient import TestClient
from streamlit.runtime.media_file_storage import MediaFileKind
from streamlit.runtime.memory_media_file_storage import MemoryMediaFileStorage
from streamlit.web.server.starlette.starlette_routes import create_media_routes

# An ordinary filename: a 5 inch by 7 inch print. The inch marks are
# double quotes, which are perfectly valid in a filename.
filename = '5" x 7" print.jpg'

storage = MemoryMediaFileStorage("/media")
file_id = storage.load_and_get_id(
    b"jpeg-bytes", "image/jpeg", MediaFileKind.DOWNLOADABLE, filename
)
client = TestClient(Starlette(routes=create_media_routes(storage, "")))
response = client.get(storage.get_url(file_id))
print(response.headers["content-disposition"])
```

The same header is produced end to end from an app, without touching internals:

```python
import streamlit as st

uploaded = st.file_uploader("upload")
if uploaded:
    # The inch marks in the file_name break the emitted header.
    st.download_button("download", data=uploaded, file_name='5" x 7" print.jpg')
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `pip install streamlit==1.61.1`
2. Save the first snippet above as `repro.py`.
3. Run `python repro.py`.
4. Observe the printed header: `attachment; filename="5" x 7" print.jpg"`. The `filename` parameter is terminated by the first `"` after `5`, so the value a conforming parser reads is not the name the app set.

### Expected Behavior

A filename with characters that are not safe unescaped inside a quoted string (a double quote, a semicolon, a space) should still be carried faithfully in a valid header, using the RFC 5987 `filename*=` form, exactly as the non-latin-1 branch already does and as Starlette's `FileResponse` does:

```
attachment; filename*=utf-8''5%22%20x%207%22%20print.jpg
```

### Current Behavior

The name is interpolated into `filename="..."` verbatim, so the double quote closes the parameter:

```
attachment; filename="5" x 7" print.jpg"
```

That is not a valid RFC 6266 header: the quoted string ends at the first unescaped `"`, and everything after it is stray tokens. A name that also contains `;` can introduce additional `Content-Disposition` parameters, so the header's structure ends up controlled by the filename rather than by Streamlit.

Root cause, `lib/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes.py` in `_media_endpoint`:

```python
try:
    filename.encode("latin1")
    disposition = f'filename="{filename}"'
except UnicodeEncodeError:
    disposition = f"filename*=utf-8''{quote(filename)}"
headers["Content-Disposition"] = f"attachment; {disposition}"
```

The branch is selected on latin-1 encodability, but the property that matters is whether the value is safe unescaped inside a quoted parameter, and `"`, `;` and space are all latin-1 encodable.

### Fix direction

Select the branch the way Starlette's `FileResponse` does in `starlette/responses.py`: emit the plain `filename="..."` form only when `quote(filename) == filename`, and fall back to `filename*=utf-8''{quote(filename)}` otherwise. This is a strict superset of the current safe branch (every non-latin-1 name still percent-encodes) and additionally routes latin-1 names that need escaping onto the safe form. Plain ASCII names like `report.pdf` keep the quoted form unchanged.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1 (present since 1.60.0; also on current `develop`)
