related_pr.title: [fix] Encode download filenames unsafe in a quoted header
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

`st.download_button` served a malformed `Content-Disposition` header whenever the filename contained a double quote. The media endpoint picked the quoted form for any latin-1 encodable name, and a `"` is latin-1, so it closed the parameter early:

```
name    : 5" x 7" print.jpg
emitted : attachment; filename="5" x 7" print.jpg"
```

Parsed by a conforming client, the filename is `5` — so the browser saves the wrong name. Three neighbouring cases in the same branch were wrong for the same reason:

| filename | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `5" x 7" print.jpg` | `filename="5" x 7" print.jpg"` → reads as `5` | `filename*=utf-8''5%22%20x%207%22%20print.jpg` |
| `a\b.txt` | `filename="a\b.txt"` → escape drops the `\` | `filename*=utf-8''a%5Cb.txt` |
| `a\r\nX-Evil: 1.txt` | CR/LF emitted into the header value raw | `filename*=utf-8''a%0D%0AX-Evil%3A%201.txt` |
| `café.pdf` | latin-1 bytes; not decodable as UTF-8 | `filename*=utf-8''caf%C3%A9.pdf` |

The branch is now selected on whether the name is genuinely safe unescaped inside a quoted string — ASCII with no quote, backslash or control character — rather than on latin-1 encodability. Anything else takes the RFC 5987 `filename*=` form that already existed for non-latin-1 names.

**Spaces and semicolons deliberately stay on the quoted path.** Neither needs escaping inside the quotes: the parameter delimiter does not apply there. Starlette's `FileResponse` uses a stricter `quote(name) == name` test, which the issue suggested adopting, but that re-encodes every filename containing a space — very common — for no correctness gain. `test_media_endpoint_downloadable_safe_filename_stays_quoted` pins the narrower behaviour, and fails if the rule is widened.

Two notes for the reviewer, both corrections to the issue writeup:

- It states existing tests cover "a space-containing quoted name". They don't — there were only two assertions, for the generated default name and the non-latin-1 branch. Nothing pinned the space case before this PR.
- It suggests a lone `;` can introduce extra header parameters. Inside the quotes it cannot, which is why `a;b.txt` is left on the quoted path.

The `café.pdf` case was not in the report. It currently raises `UnicodeDecodeError` when the response headers are read, so an ordinary accented filename is broken today too.

## GitHub Issue Link

Fixes #16631

## Testing Plan

- Unit tests in `lib/tests/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes_test.py`, driving the real media route in-process:
  - `test_media_endpoint_downloadable_filename_survives_round_trip` — parses the emitted header with `email.message.EmailMessage` and asserts the recovered filename equals the original, for the quote, backslash, latin-1-accent and non-latin-1 cases. This asserts the user-visible outcome (the saved name) rather than a header substring.
  - `test_media_endpoint_downloadable_safe_filename_stays_quoted` — `report.pdf`, `quarterly report.pdf`, `a;b.txt` keep the readable quoted form.
  - `test_media_endpoint_downloadable_filename_cannot_inject_headers` — no raw CR or LF reaches the header value.
- Mutation-verified both directions: reverting to the latin-1 branch fails the 4 round-trip/injection tests; switching to Starlette's `quote(name) == name` rule fails the 2 "stays quoted" tests.
- Full Python suite: `11387 passed, 76 skipped`. `ruff format`, `ruff check` and `ty` clean; `mypy`'s single error (`e2e_playwright/load_testing/test_load.py` unreachable statement) reproduces on unmodified `develop`.
- No frontend or protobuf surface, so no e2e coverage added.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches HTTP response headers for all downloadable media; behavior change is intentional and narrowly scoped, but wrong encoding logic would affect every `st.download_button` filename edge case.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes malformed **`Content-Disposition`** headers on the Starlette media download route when filenames contain characters that break quoted `filename="..."` values (e.g. inch marks in `5" x 7" print.jpg`), which caused browsers to save the wrong name.
> 
> **Selection logic** no longer uses “latin-1 encodable” as the gate for the quoted form. Names that are **ASCII** and free of `"`, `\`, and control characters keep the readable `filename="..."` form (including spaces and semicolons). Everything else uses **RFC 5987** `filename*=utf-8''` with **`quote(..., safe='')`** so slashes and non-ASCII names encode correctly and CR/LF cannot inject extra header lines.
> 
> **Tests** add round-trip parsing via `EmailMessage`, pin safe names on the quoted branch, and assert no raw CR/LF in the header value.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 6ed97de616d42b6406832ba3f381be0e252ad51a. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: Deck object with PointCloudLayer cannot be integrated properly with pydeck_chart
description:
# Summary

The `pydeck_chart` cannot properly integrate a Deck object with a `PointCloudLayer` without embedding a mapbox view.
The following example shows how to create a 3D point cloud layer with pydeck: https://deckgl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gallery/point_cloud_layer.html


# Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-2590)

```
import pandas as pd
import pydeck as pydeck
import streamlit as st

def main():
    DATA_URL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ajduberstein/geo_datasets/master/small_waterfall.csv"
    df = pd.read_csv(DATA_URL)

    target = [df.x.mean(), df.y.mean(), df.z.mean()]

    point_cloud_layer = pydeck.Layer(
        "PointCloudLayer",
        data=DATA_URL,
        get_position=["x", "y", "z"],
        get_color=["r", "g", "b"],
        get_normal=[0, 0, 15],
        auto_highlight=True,
        pickable=True,
        point_size=3,
    )

    view_state = pydeck.ViewState(target=target, controller=True, rotation_x=15, rotation_orbit=30, zoom=5.3)
    view = pydeck.View(type="OrbitView", controller=True)

    r = pydeck.Deck(point_cloud_layer, initial_view_state=view_state, views=[view])
    #r.to_html("point_cloud_layer.html", css_background_color="#add8e6")
    st.pydeck_chart(r)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## Expected behavior:

Using `st.pydeck_chart(r)`, I would expect a visualization of the 3D point cloud as in this example: https://deckgl.readthedocs.io/en/latest/gallery/point_cloud_layer.html 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/77327738/104307831-093f3480-54d0-11eb-885f-1e543d88e80b.png)

## Actual behavior:

- The point cloud is flat
- The map cannot be disabled
- The orbit view does not work

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/77327738/104308270-adc17680-54d0-11eb-8566-dc1e46550700.png)

## Is this a regression?

no

# Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.73.1
- Python version: 3.8.3
- Using Conda
- OS version: macOS 11.0.1
- Browser version: Chrome 87.0.4280.88 

# Additional information

With streamlit version 0.73.1 the following error appears when navigating the map (this error does not come up with streamlit version 0.69):
```
/usr/local/anaconda3/lib/python3.8/site-packages/pydeck/bindings/deck.py:105: UserWarning: Mapbox API key is not set. This may impact available features of pydeck.
  warnings.warn(
````

Related discussion:
https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/3d-data-visualization-point-clouds-and-triangular-meshes/1235

Related issue:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/809
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16819: [fix] Honor pydeck views in st.pydeck_chart.

Honor pydeck `views` in `st.pydeck_chart` so OrbitView, GlobeView, and `map_provider=None` render as specified instead of a forced 2D MapView.

- Default MapView charts still use Carto/Mapbox tiles and zoom controls.
- Apps that already passed a non-map view currently got a silent MapView fallback and will now get the requested camera.

related_pr.title: [fix] Prevent duplicate Altair bind widgets with on_select
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Skip injecting Vega-Lite encodings onto point selections that already set `fields`. That keeps Altair `binding_radio` / `binding_select` as a single widget when `on_select` is enabled, instead of duplicating binds and emptying the chart.

For single-view charts, a `fields` point selection now returns only the declared fields in the selection state, instead of those fields plus the injected chart encodings — matching what multi-view charts already returned.

Click selections that specify neither `fields` nor `encodings` still get encodings injected so they stay PointSelections rather than IndexSelections.

Vega-Lite compiles one bound input per projection, so unioning encodings onto a `fields` projection produced one radio group per encoding channel.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #8765

Related: #10308 (same encodings injection; default `value` highlight is restored, but Streamlit's returned selection dict still starts empty until a click).

## Testing Plan

- `frontend/lib/src/components/elements/ArrowVegaLiteChart/useVegaElementPreprocessor.test.ts` — fields-based params (including radio bind and scalar value) are not rewritten; shorthand point selections still get encodings; compiled Vega has one radio bind

title: mapbox.token deprecation expired 2026-05-01: logs "IS NO LONGER SUPPORTED" while the option still works
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

The `mapbox.token` config option is declared with `expiration_date="2026-05-01"`, which is now in the past. `ConfigOption.is_expired()` therefore returns `True`, and anyone who still sets the option is told it **is no longer supported** — at `ERROR` level — even though the option is still read and still works (`lib/streamlit/elements/map.py` passes it through to the PyDeck spec).

The result is a contradiction: the log says the setting has been removed, the product still honours it, and the message quotes a removal date that has already passed.

### Reproducible Code Example

`.streamlit/config.toml`:

```toml
[mapbox]
token = "pk.example"
```

Then start any app, or check the state directly:

```python
import streamlit.config as config

config.get_config_options()
opt = config._config_options_template["mapbox.token"]
print(opt.expiration_date, opt.is_expired())   # 2026-05-01 True
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Set `mapbox.token` in `config.toml` (or via `STREAMLIT_MAPBOX_TOKEN`).
2. Start the app and read the console.

### Expected Behavior

One of the following, consistently:

- The option is actually removed, and setting it is a no-op with a clear message; or
- The expiration date is moved out to a real future release, so users see the "IS DEPRECATED … will be removed on or after `<future date>`" warning instead.

### Current Behavior

```
════════════════════════════════════════════════
mapbox.token IS NO LONGER SUPPORTED.

Instead of this, you should use either the MAPBOX_API_KEY environment
variable or PyDeck's `api_keys` argument.

Please update <path to config.toml>.
════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

logged at `ERROR` level, while `config.get_option("mapbox.token")` still returns the token and `st.map` still uses it.

### Relevant Source

`lib/streamlit/config.py:1384-1398` declares the option; `lib/streamlit/config_option.py:262-297` selects the expired vs. not-expired message.

### Acceptance Criteria

### Is this a regression?

Not a regression — a deprecation that has quietly aged past its own deadline.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`, commit `2ac0d77d3`)
- Python version: 3.13.6
- Operating System: Windows 11 (platform-independent)
- Browser: n/a

### Additional Information

`mapbox.token` is currently the only deprecated option in `config.py`, so it is also the only one exercising this code path.

title: Stray 's' in config deprecation warning also disables textwrap.dedent(), leaving the message indented
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

In `ConfigOption.set_value()`, the deprecation warning for a not-yet-expired config option opens its f-string with a stray `s` character:

```python
# lib/streamlit/config_option.py:285
get_logger(__name__).warning(
    textwrap.dedent(
        f"""s
        ════════════════════════════════════════════════
        {self.key} IS DEPRECATED.
```

This has two effects. The obvious one is a literal `s` printed at the start of the warning. The subtler one is that `textwrap.dedent()` silently stops working: `dedent` strips the longest common leading whitespace across all non-blank lines, and `s` is a line with **zero** indentation, so the common prefix becomes `""` and nothing is stripped. Every subsequent line keeps its 20 spaces of source indentation.

The sibling "expired" branch a few lines above is written correctly and dedents as intended, which makes the difference easy to see side by side.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import logging

from streamlit.config_option import ConfigOption

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s|%(message)s")

opt = ConfigOption(
    "test.notexpired",
    description="d",
    default_val="",
    deprecated=True,
    deprecation_text="Use something else.",
    expiration_date="2999-01-01",
)
opt.set_value("x", "some_file.toml")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the snippet above (any deprecated config option whose `expiration_date` is in the future takes this branch).
2. Compare the output with the expired branch (set `expiration_date="2020-01-01"`).

### Expected Behavior

The warning should be flush-left and free of stray characters, matching the expired-option message:

```
════════════════════════════════════════════════
test.notexpired IS DEPRECATED.
Use something else.

This option will be removed on or after 2999-01-01.

Please update some_file.toml.
════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

### Current Behavior

```
WARNING streamlit.config_option: s
                    ════════════════════════════════════════════════
                    test.notexpired IS DEPRECATED.
                    Use something else.

                    This option will be removed on or after 2999-01-01.

                    Please update some_file.toml.
                    ════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

For contrast, the expired branch on the same run is correct:

```
ERROR streamlit.config_option:
════════════════════════════════════════════════
test.expired IS NO LONGER SUPPORTED.

Use something else.

Please update some_file.toml.
════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

### Suggested Fix

Delete the stray `s` so the first line is empty and `dedent()` can compute the correct common prefix.

### Acceptance Criteria

### Is this a regression?

Unknown.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`, commit `2ac0d77d3`)
- Python version: 3.13.6
- Operating System: Windows 11 (platform-independent)
- Browser: n/a

### Additional Information

This branch is currently hard to hit in practice because the only deprecated option in `config.py` (`mapbox.token`) is already past its expiration date and therefore takes the *other* branch — see the companion issue about that expiry. Any newly added deprecation would surface this immediately.

title: Element values are not restored properly after `st.rerun`
description: ### Summary Values of components which appear after `st.experimental_rerun()` are not restored but initialized after executing `st.experimental_rerun()` ### Steps to reproduce Code snippet: [![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-3533) ```python import streamlit as st radio_value = st.radio("Select1", ["Egg", "Spam", "Bacon", "Sausage"]) st.write(radio_value) if st.button("Rerun"): st.experimental_rerun() radio_value = st.radio("Select2", ["Egg", "Spam", "Bacon", "Sausage"]) st.write(radio_value) radio_value = st.radio("Select3", ["Egg", "Spam", "Bacon", "Sausage"]) st.write(radio_value) ``` 1. At first, all radio values are "Egg" 2. Change the selections; for example, "Spam", "Bacon", and "Sausage" for 3 radios respectively. title: st.file_uploader hangs indefinitely on small files when sentry_sdk.init() runs in-process before Streamlit starts
description:
**Summary**

File uploads under ~10KB hang indefinitely (eventually timing out client-side) when `sentry_sdk.init()` is called in the same process, before Streamlit's own event loop is created, and Streamlit is then started in that process (e.g. via `streamlit.web.cli.main()` after rewriting `sys.argv`, rather than a fresh `streamlit run` subprocess). Uploads over ~10KB are unaffected. This reproduces with no application code beyond a single `st.file_uploader()`.

This in-process launch pattern is common for wrapper entrypoints that do setup (init error tracking, run DB migrations, etc.) before starting Streamlit without spawning a new OS process.

**Reproducible Code Example**

```python
"""
pip install streamlit==1.61.1 sentry-sdk==2.61.1
python repro.py
Then open http://localhost:8501 and upload a file smaller than ~10KB.
"""
import sys
import pathlib

pathlib.Path("app.py").write_text('''
import streamlit as st
uploaded = st.file_uploader("pick a file")
if uploaded is not None:
    st.write(f"Got {uploaded.name}, {len(uploaded.getvalue())} bytes")
''')

import sentry_sdk
sentry_sdk.init(dsn=None)  # comment this line out and the hang disappears

from streamlit.web import cli
sys.argv = ["streamlit", "run", "app.py"]
sys.exit(cli.main())
```

**Steps To Reproduce**

1. `pip install streamlit==1.61.1 sentry-sdk==2.61.1`
2. Save the snippet above as `repro.py`, run `python repro.py`
3. Open `http://localhost:8501`, upload any file smaller than ~10KB (e.g. a 300-byte CSV)
4. Upload hangs indefinitely. Comment out `sentry_sdk.init(dsn=None)` and it succeeds instantly. Upload a file larger than ~10KB and it succeeds either way.

**Expected Behavior**

Upload completes regardless of file size or whether Sentry was initialized in-process before Streamlit started.

**Current Behavior**

Small uploads hang. Root-caused to Sentry's `StarletteIntegration` (enabled by default) — confirmed via `sentry_sdk.init(dsn=None, disabled_integrations=[StarletteIntegration()])` (succeeds) vs. `disabled_integrations=[ThreadingIntegration()]` (still hangs — ruling out threading despite superficial similarity to #15374 / #16139, both of which are already fixed in this version and don't apply since this repro has no `st.fragment(run_every=...)`). `StarletteIntegration` instruments Starlette's ASGI request lifecycle, and the hang lives inside Starlette's own multipart parser — Sentry wraps exactly the layer that breaks.

**Is this a regression?**

Not tested on older versions — can test if useful.

**Debug info**

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: 3.12
- OS: macOS (also reproduces in a Linux container)
- sentry-sdk version: 2.61.1

**Additional Information**

Fuller repro with isolation scripts (control, all-integrations-disabled, Starlette-only-disabled) and sample CSVs: https://gist.github.com/tbrambor/d41b40950a0061ca404fc0d67e4768ed
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16709: [fix] Prevent upload hang when middleware reads the body first.

related_pr.title: [fix] Prevent upload hang when middleware reads the body first
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Prevent uploads from hanging when in-process ASGI middleware, including Sentry, has already cached the request body — leaving a file chip spinning forever, or a chat submit button permanently disabled. The upload handler now reads the original request's cache-aware `stream()` while retaining its size cap; a body consumed without caching or replaying returns 400 and logs the likely cause.

Regression from #16207 (1.61.0): wrapping the raw ASGI `receive()` channel left uploads hung when a layer such as Sentry's `StarletteIntegration` had already called `body()` on the same `Request` (default capture cutoff ~10 KB). Before #16207 the handler called `await request.form()` on the original request, which is cache-aware.

Reproduced on `st.file_uploader` and on `st.chat_input` attachments; `st.camera_input` and `st.audio_input` share the same `/_stcore/upload_file` route.

- End-of-body comes from generator exhaustion rather than an empty chunk, so framing does not depend on how `stream()` chunks an empty tail across `starlette>=0.46.0,<2`.
- Only `RuntimeError("Stream consumed")` maps to 400; any other channel `RuntimeError` keeps its 500 so operators are not sent after the wrong cause.
- Rejected Starlette's native `form(max_part_size=...)`: `MultiPartParser.on_part_data` size-checks only the non-file branch, so file parts are unchecked and that path would have silently dropped #16207's protection rather than merely weakening it.

**What this does not fix:** a layer that drains the channel without replaying it downstream still hangs. The bytes are gone, and the handler cannot distinguish "no more body" from "body still in flight" without a disconnect. Buffer-and-replay middleware was never affected.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

Fixes #16697. Upstream counterpart: [getsentry/sentry-python#7285](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-python/issues/7285) — worth fixing here regardless, since that addresses one trigger rather than the pattern.

## Testing Plan

- **Unit Tests (Python)** — regression tests in `starlette_routes_test.py`, each verified to fail against the unfixed handler: upload succeeds after a middleware cached the body (asserting the raw channel is touched exactly once), the size cap still fires on a cached body, an un-cached consumed body returns 400, and an unrelated channel `RuntimeError` keeps its 500. A parametrized multi-chunk case covers the reconstructed ASGI framing, which the pre-existing chunked test only exercised on the 413 abort path.
- **E2E Tests** — `test_mega_tester_app_uploads_small_file` drives `/_stcore/upload_file` in external app mode, which nothing previously covered. It asserts terminal widget state (spinner absent), not just the chip name, since the chip renders while the PUT is still in flight. Verified against a deliberately stalled upload: the chip-name assertion alone passes, the spinner assertion fails. **Verified in local mode only** — external mode needs a hosted URL, so behavior against a real deployment is unconfirmed. Separate commit so it can be dropped if reviewers would rather land it after seeing external CI.
- Verified end to end with the reporter's own launch pattern (in-process `sentry_sdk.init()`, then `cli.main()`), driving a real browser against the full server: the sub-10KB upload that previously hung now completes. Confirmed on sentry-sdk 2.61.1 (the reported version) and 2.68.1, and on starlette 0.46.0 (the dependency floor) as well as 1.6.0.
- Manual QA against the live trigger, each case run with and without the fix: `st.file_uploader` and `st.chat_input` attachments both hang before and succeed after; `st.camera_input` capture uploads successfully after. Separately, since the framing change affects every upload rather than only the middleware case, checked a 4.9 MB upload (many real chunks), three files in one interaction, and an oversized upload against `server.maxUploadSize` — the last surfaces an error chip with no spinner left behind, rather than stalling.

Note on scope: triggering this requires an **in-process** ASGI layer. Reverse proxies, ingress, and WAFs cannot cause it — they forward a complete request, so uvicorn builds a fresh `receive()` channel. Snowflake's warehouse runtime is also unaffected, since it drives `Runtime` directly rather than through `streamlit.web.server`.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core upload parsing for every PUT to `/_stcore/upload_file`; behavior is well-covered by new tests but affects a security-sensitive path (size limits, multipart handling).
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#16697**: `st.file_uploader` (and other widgets using `/_stcore/upload_file`) could hang indefinitely when in-process ASGI middleware such as Sentry’s Starlette integration had already read the request body. A regression from wrapping the raw `receive()` channel meant the upload handler blocked on an exhausted stream while keep-alive stayed open.
> 
> The **PUT upload handler** now drives multipart parsing from the original request’s cache-aware `request.stream()`, rebuilding ASGI messages with the existing **streaming `server.maxUploadSize` cap** intact. Bodies that were streamed away without caching get a **400** plus a server log instead of hanging; only Starlette’s `"Stream consumed"` `RuntimeError` is mapped that way.
> 
> **Tests:** new unit regressions for cached-body success, multi-chunk bodies, size limits on cached bodies, and consumed-stream failures; a Playwright **external** test uploads a tiny CSV and asserts the file chip finishes (no spinner, no alert).
>

title: `AppTest.switch_page()` cannot navigate to an `st.navigation` page that sets a custom `url_path`
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

`AppTest.switch_page(page_path)` computes the target page hash from the page's **file
name**. But `st.navigation` identifies each `st.Page` by its **`url_path`**. When a page
sets a custom `url_path` that differs from its file name, the two hashes disagree:
`switch_page` sets a `_page_hash` that matches no registered page, and the script runner
**silently falls back to the default page** instead of navigating to the requested one (and
without raising).

This makes it impossible to test navigation to any page declared like
`st.Page("other.py", url_path="custom")`.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
See below.
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Files (all in one directory):

`home.py`
```python
import streamlit as st

st.write("HOME PAGE")
```

`other.py`
```python
import streamlit as st

st.write("OTHER PAGE")
```

`app.py`
```python
import streamlit as st

home = st.Page("home.py", default=True)
other = st.Page("other.py", url_path="custom")  # url_path != file name ("other")

st.navigation([home, other]).run()
```

`test_switch_page.py`
```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

def test_switch_to_page_with_custom_url_path():
    at = AppTest.from_file("app.py").run()
    assert at.markdown[0].value == "HOME PAGE"

    at.switch_page("other.py").run()

    assert at.markdown[0].value == "OTHER PAGE"  # FAILS: is "HOME PAGE"
```

Run pytest:
```
$ pytest test_switch_page.py
E       AssertionError: assert 'HOME PAGE' == 'OTHER PAGE'
```

### Expected Behavior

`at.switch_page("other.py").run()` renders the `other` page (or, if the path can't be resolved to a registered page, raises a clear error).

### Current Behavior

The default page is rendered, silently.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.61.1
- Python version: 3.13.15
- Operating System: Linux (WSL2) — also expected on macOS/Windows; not platform-specific

### Additional Information

#### Root cause

`AppTest.switch_page` derives the hash from the file name
(`streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py`):

```python
page_path_str = str(full_page_path.resolve())
_, page_name = page_icon_and_name(Path(page_path_str))
self._page_hash = calc_hash(page_name)          # hash of the FILE NAME
```

but `st.navigation` registers each page under a hash derived from its `url_path`
(`streamlit/navigation/page.py`):

```python
@property
def _script_hash(self) -> str:
    return calc_hash(self._url_path)             # hash of the URL PATH
```

`self._url_path` defaults to the file-name-derived slug, so the two hashes coincide **only
when `url_path` is not overridden**. With a custom `url_path`, `calc_hash(page_name)`
matches no registered page, so the runner uses the default page instead.

#### Suggested fix

Resolve the requested page against the app's registered navigation pages (via the
`PagesManager` / `st.navigation` result), matching by resolved script path, and use that
page's actual `_script_hash` (which respects `url_path`) for `_page_hash`. Because the
navigation config is only known once the app runs, this can be done by deferring resolution
to the next `run()` (store the requested path in `switch_page`, resolve it against the
freshly built pages when running).

At minimum — even without full resolution — `switch_page`/`run` should **raise a clear
error when the computed hash matches no registered page**, rather than silently rendering
the default page, so the failure is not hidden from test authors.

#### Workaround

Set `_page_hash` to the `url_path`-based hash directly for the affected pages:

```python
from streamlit.util import calc_hash

at._page_hash = calc_hash("custom")  # the page's url_path
at.run()
```

resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16706: [fix] Show the correct year in the date picker header.

related_pr.title: [fix] Show the correct year in the date picker header
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

The date and datetime calendar header now builds its year options from the widget's own bounds, so the header year matches the grid when `min_value` and `max_value` cross a year boundary.

React Aria's `CalendarYearPicker` stepped whole years from `minValue`, dropping the final year whenever `maxValue`'s month/day fell earlier in the year, and its `value` is an index that then silently falls back to the first entry. With `min_value=date(2024, 8, 3)` and `max_value=date(2025, 2, 3)`, the grid showed February 2025 while the header read 2024 and the dropdown offered only 2024.

The dropdown still offers 20 years at a time, matching React Aria's `visibleYears` default, but the window is now anchored on the focused year and slid inside the bounds rather than starting at `min_value`. With default bounds (`value ± 10 years`) the resulting list is unchanged; for wide explicit bounds it shifts which 20 years appear.

Two further defects surfaced while fixing that and are addressed here:

- **Non-Gregorian locales.** The visitor's locale selects the calendar system, so `focusedDate` may be Buddhist or Persian while `minValue`/`maxValue` arrive Gregorian. The bounds are converted before their years are read — otherwise Thai and Persian visitors get a blank year trigger on every `st.date_input`, including with default bounds.
- **Unreachable months.** Every month was offered regardless of the bounds, and picking one relocated the calendar to the nearest bound: ask for January, land in August. Months holding no selectable day are now disabled and faded, matching how the day grid already renders unreachable dates. Partly reachable months stay selectable — with `max_value` 2025-02-03, February still offers the 1st through the 3rd.

`CalendarYearPicker` stays mounted for its localized `aria-label`, so the workaround reverts cleanly once the upstream fix lands.

Affects `st.date_input` (single and range) and `st.datetime_input`, which share the calendar header.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

Closes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16686

Upstream issue filed for the root cause: https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10531

## Testing Plan

- **Frontend unit tests** — boundary-year listing across bound shapes, non-Gregorian trigger/grid agreement (`th`, `fa-IR`), the visible-year window cap, month availability, clamping when a picked year leaves the range, and range mode's separate calendar state.
- **E2E tests** — `st_date_input_test.py` and `st_datetime_input_test.py`, asserting header text, option lists, and that unreachable months are styled as unreachable rather than only marked `aria-disabled`.
- Verified the new tests fail without the fix: 5 against the pre-fix header, and 2 more that specifically cover the non-Gregorian conversion.
- Manual testing: covered by the unit and E2E cases above, plus an automated QA pass (25 scenarios, including `th`/`fa-IR` locales) against a debug server.


---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Widget-only frontend calendar UX with extensive tests; no auth, persistence, or API contract changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#16686** by replacing React Aria’s year dropdown logic in `CalendarPopoverHeader` with a bounds-aware list: a 20-year window anchored on the focused year, both boundary years included when `min_value`/`max_value` span a year with “earlier” month/day on the max side, and the header label aligned with the grid instead of falling back to the first option.
> 
> **Also in this change:** convert `min`/`max` years into the visitor’s calendar before building options (fixes blank year triggers for locales like Thai/Persian); mark months with no selectable days as disabled with faded/`not-allowed` styling so choosing them no longer jumps the view to a bound; year selection updates only the year and keeps the focused month.
> 
> Applies to **`st.date_input`** (single and range) and **`st.datetime_input`** via the shared header. Coverage adds unit tests, Playwright scenarios for year-crossing bounds, and e2e demo widgets.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 8488e47497d94c9e6a2c6dd57d92369207eb1478. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: StreamlitInvalidColorError message renders as one run-on line because bullets lack newlines
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

`StreamlitInvalidColorError` builds its message from implicitly concatenated string literals, but the literals that introduce the bullet list have no separating newline:

```python
# lib/streamlit/errors.py:589-592
"This does not look like a valid color: {color}.\n\n"
"Colors must be in one of the following formats:"
"* Hex string with 3, 4, 6, or 8 digits. Example: `'#00ff00'`"
"* List or tuple with 3 or 4 components. Example: `[1.0, 0.5, 0, 0.2]`",
```

Python concatenates these into a single line, so the two bullets never start a new line. Because the message is rendered as Markdown, the `*` characters do not become a list — they appear as literal asterisks mid-sentence.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.map(
    {"lat": [37.77], "lon": [-122.4]},
    color="not-a-color",
)
```

Or directly:

```python
from streamlit.elements.lib.color_util import to_int_color_tuple

to_int_color_tuple("red")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Pass any invalid color to an API that validates colors (`st.map(color=...)`, `st.scatter_chart(color=...)`, etc.).
2. Read the resulting error message.

### Expected Behavior

```
This does not look like a valid color: 'red'.

Colors must be in one of the following formats:
* Hex string with 3, 4, 6, or 8 digits. Example: `'#00ff00'`
* List or tuple with 3 or 4 components. Example: `[1.0, 0.5, 0, 0.2]`
```

### Current Behavior

```
This does not look like a valid color: 'red'.

Colors must be in one of the following formats:* Hex string with 3, 4, 6, or 8 digits. Example: `'#00ff00'`* List or tuple with 3 or 4 components. Example: `[1.0, 0.5, 0, 0.2]`
```

### Suggested Fix

Append `\n` to the `"...following formats:"` literal and to the first bullet.

### Acceptance Criteria

### Is this a regression?

Unknown.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`, commit `2ac0d77d3`)
- Python version: 3.13.6
- Operating System: Windows 11 (platform-independent)
- Browser: n/a

### Additional Information

I scanned the rest of `lib/streamlit/` for the same pattern (a string literal beginning `* ` or `- ` immediately following a literal that does not end in a newline) using a `tokenize`-based check; `errors.py:591-592` is the only occurrence, so this looks like an isolated slip rather than a systemic one.

title: is_mem_address_str() fails on uppercase hex addresses, breaking st.write() and st.help() object rendering on Windows
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

`is_mem_address_str()` in `lib/streamlit/string_util.py` matches memory-address reprs with the regex `^\<[a-zA-Z_]+[a-zA-Z0-9<>._ ]* at 0x[0-9a-f]+\>$`. The address group only accepts **lowercase** hex digits. On Windows, CPython formats object addresses with **uppercase** hex (e.g. `<__main__.Foo object at 0x0000027B0C1B1550>`), so the function returns `False` for essentially every real object repr on that platform.

Both callers of this helper then take the wrong branch: `st.write(obj)` stops routing plain objects to the object-help view and prints the raw memory address instead, and `st.help()` renders memory addresses as member values while dropping those members' docstrings.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

class Foo:
    """A Foo."""

    x = 1

    @property
    def e(self):
        "Property e"
        return 5

st.write(Foo())   # expected: rich object-help view. On Windows: raw memory address as inline code.
st.help(Foo)      # expected: property `e` documented. On Windows: "<property object at 0x...>".
```

Minimal check of the helper itself:

```python
from streamlit.string_util import is_mem_address_str

class Foo:
    pass

print(repr(Foo()))                  # <__main__.Foo object at 0x0000023FFDF98AD0>
print(is_mem_address_str(repr(Foo())))          # False   <-- should be True
print(is_mem_address_str("<foo blarg at 0x15ee6f9a0>"))  # True (lowercase only)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. On Windows, run either snippet above (or just the plain-Python helper check — no browser needed).
2. Observe that `is_mem_address_str` returns `False` for a repr it is explicitly designed to detect.

### Expected Behavior

`is_mem_address_str()` should recognize a CPython memory-address repr regardless of the hex casing produced by the platform's C runtime. Consequently:

- `st.write(obj)` renders the object-help view for an object with no other special handling.
- `st.help(SomeClass)` shows the property's docstring and leaves the value slot empty rather than printing a memory address.

### Current Behavior

On Windows (verified with `AppTest`):

```
markdown elements: ['`<__main__.Foo object at 0x0000027B0C1B1550>`']
help elements    : 0
```

`st.help` on a class with a `@property`:

```
name='e' type='property' value='<property object at 0x000002500A1F3240>' doc=''
```

versus the same class instance, which takes the other code path and is correct:

```
name='e' type='property' value='' doc='Property e'
```

The repository's own tests catch this — they currently fail on Windows for exactly this reason:

- `lib/tests/streamlit/write_test.py::StreamlitWriteTest::test_obj_instance` → `AssertionError: Expected 'help' to be called once. Called 0 times.`
- `lib/tests/streamlit/write_test.py::StreamlitWriteTest::test_repr_html`
- `lib/tests/streamlit/write_test.py::StreamlitWriteTest::test_repr_html_no_html_tags_in_string`
- `lib/tests/streamlit/write_test.py::StreamlitWriteTest::test_repr_html_not_callable`
- `lib/tests/streamlit/elements/help_test.py::StHelpTest::test_class_members` → `assert '<property ob...>' == ''`

They pass on Linux/macOS because glibc's `%p` formatting yields lowercase hex, which is why CI has not caught it.

### Root Cause

`lib/streamlit/string_util.py:250-252`

```python
_OBJ_MEM_ADDRESS: Final = re.compile(
    r"^\<[a-zA-Z_]+[a-zA-Z0-9<>._ ]* at 0x[0-9a-f]+\>$"
)
```

`[0-9a-f]+` cannot match `0000027B0C1B1550`.

### Suggested Fix

Accept both casings, e.g. `[0-9a-fA-F]+` (or add `re.IGNORECASE`).

### Acceptance Criteria

### Is this a regression?

Unknown — the regex appears long-standing.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`, commit `2ac0d77d3`)
- Python version: 3.13.6
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: n/a (reproduced headlessly via `streamlit.testing.v1.AppTest` and direct function calls)

### Additional Information

The two affected call sites are `lib/streamlit/elements/help.py:482` and `lib/streamlit/elements/write.py:576`.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16683: [fix] Error message bullets and uppercase-hex object reprs.

CPython formats the address with the platform C runtime's `%p`, and MSVC yields `0x0000027B0C1B1550` — which made `st.write()` print a raw address instead of the object-help view, and `st.help()` render `<property object at 0x...>` as a member value while dropping that member's docstring. Uses a character class rather than `re.IGNORECASE`, which would also let `" AT 0X"` match; a negative test pins that.

title: Python unit tests are not portable to Windows (path separators, NamedTemporaryFile reopen, registry-dependent MIME type)
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

Running the Python unit suite on Windows produces a large number of failures that are caused by the tests themselves rather than by the library. `CONTRIBUTING.md` does not restrict development to POSIX, so a contributor on Windows currently cannot use a green suite as a baseline.

This report covers three failures whose root cause I isolated precisely. (Two other clusters are excluded on purpose: the `write_test.py` / `help_test.py` failures belong to a separate library bug I filed about `is_mem_address_str`, and the `metrics_util_test.py` cluster is caused by the tests reading the developer's real home directory, which is a distinct test-isolation concern.)

### Steps To Reproduce

```console
$ uv run pytest lib/tests/ -q
```

on Windows.

### Failures and root causes

**1. `lib/tests/streamlit/components/v2/test_component_registry.py::test_resolve_glob_pattern_direct`**

The assertion compares a native path string against a POSIX-normalized one:

```python
assert str(resolved.resolve()) == Path(test_file).resolve().as_posix()
```

`str(Path)` yields `C:\Users\...\test-pattern.js` while `.as_posix()` yields `C:/Users/.../test-pattern.js`. These coincide only on POSIX.

```
AssertionError: assert 'C:\\Users\\a...st-pattern.js' == 'C:/Users/asu...st-pattern.js'
```

Fix: compare like with like — either `.as_posix()` on both sides or `Path(...) == Path(...)`.

**2. `lib/tests/streamlit/elements/video_test.py::VideoTest::test_st_video_subtitles_path`**

The test writes to a `NamedTemporaryFile` and, while it is still open, passes its path to `st.video(...)`, which reopens it. Windows does not permit reopening a still-open `NamedTemporaryFile`:

```
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: 'C:\\Users\\...\\tmpyltckifk.vtt'
lib\streamlit\elements\lib\subtitle_utils.py:121: PermissionError
```

Fix: close the handle (or use `delete=False` / a `TemporaryDirectory`) before handing the path to code that opens it.

**3. `lib/tests/streamlit/elements/download_button_test.py::DownloadButtonTest::test_file_object_infers_file_name_and_mime`**

The test asserts a specific MIME type for `.csv`:

```
AssertionError: assert 'application/vnd.ms-excel' == 'text/csv'
```

`mimetypes.guess_type()` consults the Windows registry (`HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT`), where `.csv` is commonly mapped to `application/vnd.ms-excel` on machines with Excel installed. The expected value therefore depends on the host's registry rather than on Streamlit.

Fix: register the expected mapping in the test (or in library setup) via `mimetypes.add_type("text/csv", ".csv")`, or assert against `mimetypes.guess_type` rather than a hard-coded string.

### Expected Behavior

`uv run pytest lib/tests/` passes on Windows, or the supported development platforms are stated explicitly in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### Current Behavior

A full run reports **59 distinct test failures (95 including subtests)**, of which the three above are cleanly attributable to non-portable test code.

### Acceptance Criteria

### Is this a regression?

Unknown.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.62.0 (`develop`, commit `2ac0d77d3`)
- Python version: 3.13.6
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: n/a

### Additional Information

Happy to split these into separate issues or open a PR for the three fixes if that is preferred.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16685: [chore] Make three unit tests pass on Windows.

related_pr.title: [chore] Make three unit tests pass on Windows
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Make three Python unit tests host-independent so they pass on native Windows.

- `test_resolve_glob_pattern_direct` compared a native-separator string to an `as_posix()` string. That assertion is wrong on every platform and passed on POSIX only because the two forms coincide there; it now compares `Path` objects.
- `test_st_video_subtitles_path` called `st.video()` while its `NamedTemporaryFile` was still open, and subtitle handling reopens that path — Windows creates the file with exclusive access, so the reopen raised `PermissionError`. Now uses `TemporaryDirectory`, so nothing is reopened while open.
- `download_button_test` asserted inferred mime types that come from `mimetypes`, which reads the registry on Windows — where an installed app can claim an extension (Excel maps `.csv` to `application/vnd.ms-excel`). `setUp` now pins `.csv`, `.json`, and `.png`, so the assertions cover Streamlit's inference rather than the host. A lookup in `setUpClass` binds `types_map` to the dict `guess_type` reads, without the `add_type()` registrations that `init()` would discard.

No Windows CI job is added. The "Windows" section of `CONTRIBUTING.md` states the development setup is Mac- and Linux-centric and directs Windows contributors to the devcontainer, WSL, or a VM, and the issue lists such a job as optional. Other Windows-only failures remain out of scope; #16674 tracks the `is_mem_address_str` cluster affecting `st.write` and `st.help`.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

Fixes #16679

## Testing Plan

- Unit Tests (Python): the changed tests are the coverage. None of them weakens what it asserts — each still fails if inference doesn't run or resolves the wrong path.
- E2E Tests: none. Test-only change with no library code.
- Any manual testing needed? No. Verified without a Windows machine by reproducing each failure mode locally: `PureWindowsPath` shows the old path assertion evaluates to `False` under Windows separators, and installing the Windows registry mappings in-process reproduces the exact reported failures (`assert 'application/vnd.ms-excel' == 'text/csv'`, `assert 'image/pjpeg' == 'image/png'`), which the pin resolves.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Test-only changes with no production code; risk is limited to test maintenance and does not affect runtime behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes three unit tests that failed on native Windows due to host-specific path, file locking, and MIME registry behavior. **No library code changes.**
> 
> **Glob path assertion** in `test_resolve_glob_pattern_direct` now compares resolved `Path` objects instead of a native-path string against an `as_posix()` string, which only matched on POSIX.
> 
> **Download button MIME tests** pin `mimetypes.types_map` for `.csv`, `.json`, and `.png` in `setUp` (with `setUpClass` priming `guess_type` so the patch applies), so assertions test Streamlit’s inference rather than Windows registry overrides (e.g. Excel mapping `.csv` to `application/vnd.ms-excel`).
> 
> **Video subtitle path test** writes the VTT under `TemporaryDirectory` and closes the file before `st.video`, avoiding `PermissionError` when subtitle handling reopens the path while a `NamedTemporaryFile` is still open on Windows.
>

title: Typing issue for `st.selectbox` when `index: int | None` & `accept_new_options=False`
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

Hello!

When I use `st.selectbox` with an dynamic index which can be `int | None`, with the default for `accept_new_options` (so should be False), the return type includes `str`, so gives `T | str | None` instead of `T | None`...

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
from typing_extensions import assert_type

index: int | None = None

result = st.selectbox(
    "Entity",
    [1, 2, 3],
    index=index,
    # accept_new_options=False, # default is False anyway
)
assert_type(result, int | None)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. setup a venv with `streamlit` (1.62.0) & `pyrefly` (1.2.0)
2. run `pyrefly check ./repro-file.py`
3. notice the error: (first line)
```
ERROR assert_type(int | str | None, int | None) failed [assert-type]
  --> main.py:12:12
   |
12 | assert_type(result, int | None)
   |            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
 INFO 1 error
```

### Expected Behavior

Typing should be `T | None` since I have `accept_new_options=False` (the default), so the return can never be a `str` AFAIK 🤔..

### Current Behavior

Typing gives `T | str | None`

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: found in 1.52.2 , but this example was tested on 1.62.0
- Python version: python 3.12
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: N/A

### Additional Information

Interestingly `mypy` doesn't report any typing error here, maybe it's less capable for this overload? 🤔
Or maybe this is a `pyrefly` bug?
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16633: [fix] Correct public widget overload typings.

related_pr.title: [fix] Correct public widget overload typings
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Corrects public `@overload` signatures so type checkers infer the documented return types when arguments are omitted or not literals.

- `st.plotly_chart` / `st.pydeck_chart`: omitting `on_select` now infers `DeltaGenerator`, matching the `"ignore"` default and the pattern already used by `st.dataframe` and `st.altair_chart`. Code that used the result as `PlotlyState`/`PydeckState` without `on_select` will now fail type checking — it was already an `AttributeError` at runtime.
- `st.file_uploader` / `st.chat_input`: fallback overloads cover non-literal `bool` discriminators, which mypy does not expand into `Literal[True] | Literal[False]`.
- `st.selectbox`: a dynamic `index: int | None` no longer picks up a spurious `| str` from the `accept_new_options: bool` catch-all.
- `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`: `required=True` with `selection_mode="multi"` is now a type error instead of only a runtime `StreamlitAPIException`. A non-literal `required` now resolves in single-select mode. A `required: bool` variable with `"multi"` also no longer matches an overload (inherent: `bool` cannot reject `True`).
- `st.number_input`: omitting `value` infers `int`/`float` rather than leaving the TypeVar unsolved.

Users upgrading may see new type errors in unchanged code for the cases above. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16630

## Testing Plan

- Python typing tests in `lib/tests/streamlit/typing/` cover literal, fallback, and mixed-parameter cases for the affected commands.
- CI enforces these via `make python-types`. Unused `# type: ignore[call-overload]` entries are errors (`warn_unused_ignores`), so the negative assertions for invalid `required=True` + `"multi"` combinations are real.
- No E2E or runtime unit tests: implementation bodies are unchanged.

title: Guest-to-host messages are only posted to window.parent, so a same-window embed host never receives them (METRICS_EVENT is dropped)
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

`HostCommunicationManager.sendMessageToHost` posts only to `window.parent`. When Streamlit is
embedded such that the host code runs *in the app's own window* (an in-iframe embed
preamble/adapter, rather than in the parent frame), no guest-to-host message reaches the host,
because `window.parent` is a third-party page in this case.

`GUEST_READY` is the one exception: `openHostCommunication` additionally posts it to the app's
own window. Every other message, notably `METRICS_EVENT`, has no such path, so embedded apps
report app-load state correctly but emit **no metrics at all** to the host.

Notably, the library already assumes this topology in the opposite direction:
`receiveHostMessage` explicitly trusts same-window self-posts, with the comment
"an in-iframe embed preamble ... when there is no trusted parent frame to relay them
(`window.parent` is a third-party page)". Only the guest-to-host direction is missing it.

### Root cause

`frontend/lib/src/hostComm/HostCommunicationManager.tsx`

```ts
// :186 — parent only
public sendMessageToHost = (message: IGuestToHostMessage): void => {
  window.parent.postMessage(this.buildVersionedMessage(message), "*")
}

// :116-121 — the only same-window dispatch, GUEST_READY exclusive
if (window !== window.parent) {
  window.postMessage(this.buildVersionedMessage(guestReadyMessage), window.location.origin)
}
```

`MetricsManager` is working correctly: with `metricsUrl === "postMessage"` it takes the
`postMessageEvent` branch and calls `sendMessageToHost`. The event is built and sent: it is
simply delivered to a window the host isn't in.

### Proposed fix

Move the same-window dispatch into `sendMessageToHost` so it applies to all guest-to-host
messages, and delete the now-redundant `GUEST_READY` block in `openHostCommunication`:

```ts
public sendMessageToHost = (message: IGuestToHostMessage): void => {
  const versionedMessage = this.buildVersionedMessage(message)
  window.parent.postMessage(versionedMessage, "*")
  // An in-window embed host cannot see a post to the third-party parent.
  if (window !== window.parent) {
    // Tagged so the echo is not executed as a host command (e.g. UPDATE_HASH).
    window.postMessage(
      { ...versionedMessage, isGuestToHostEcho: true },
      window.location.origin
    )
  }
}
```

and drop the echo early in `receiveHostMessage`:

```ts
// Our own echo (see sendMessageToHost), not an inbound host command.
if ((event.data as { isGuestToHostEcho?: boolean })?.isGuestToHostEcho) {
  return
}
```

### Alternatives considered

- Retarget to `window` when embedded — rejected, breaks parent-frame hosts (above).
- Echo only `METRICS_EVENT` — narrower and avoids the collision entirely, but leaves the same
  gap for every other message type.
- Have `receiveHostMessage` ignore all self-posts — not possible; it relies on trusting them
  for host-to-guest delivery (e.g. `SET_AUTH_TOKEN`).

### Version

- Reproduced against `develop` (`frontend/package.json` 1.62.0); observed in a deployed 1.58.0
  frontend.
- Browser: Chrome 142.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python

```

### Steps To Reproduce

https://docs.snowflake.com/en/LIMITEDACCESS/streamlit/embed-streamlit-app

1. Embed a Streamlit app in a cross-origin page, with host code running inside the app's own
   window (i.e. the host listens via `window.addEventListener("message", ...)` in the app frame,
   not in the parent).
2. Set `metricsUrl: "postMessage"` in the host config and leave `browser.gatherUsageStats` at
   its default (`true`).
3. Attach listeners in both the parent frame and the app's own window and load the app.

**Expected:** the in-window host receives `METRICS_EVENT` (`viewReport`, `updateReport`,
`pageProfile`) along with the other guest-to-host messages.

**Actual:** only the *parent* frame receives them. The in-window host receives `GUEST_READY`
and nothing else.

### Expected Behavior

When Streamlit is embedded such that the host code runs inside the app's own window (an
in-iframe embed preamble/adapter rather than code in the parent frame), the host should receive
all guest-to-host messages — including METRICS_EVENT (`viewReport`, `updateReport`,
`pageProfile`) when the host config sets `metricsUrl: "postMessage"`.

### Current Behavior

`sendMessageToHost` posts only to `window.parent`, which in the embedding case is the third-party
embedding page and not the host. So the in-window host receives nothing.

The single exception is GUEST_READY, which `openHostCommunication` additionally posts to the
app's own window. The result is that app-load/readiness signalling works, while every other
message is silently invisible to the host, most visibly METRICS_EVENT, so embedded apps report
no usage metrics at all despite `browser.gatherUsageStats` being true and `metricsUrl` being
correctly set to "postMessage".

Confirmed by attaching `message` listeners to both frames: `viewReport`, `updateReport` and
`pageProfile` all arrive at the parent frame, and only GUEST_READY arrives in the app's own
window. MetricsManager itself behaves correctly: it takes the `postMessageEvent` branch and
builds the event; the message is just delivered to a window the host is not in.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

### Additional Information

_No response_
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16647: [fix] Echo guest-to-host messages to in-iframe hosts.

related_pr.title: [fix] Echo guest-to-host messages to in-iframe hosts
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Echoes every guest-to-host `postMessage` to the app window when Streamlit is embedded (`window !== window.parent`), so in-iframe hosts (parent is a third-party page) receive the full stream — not only `GUEST_READY`. That unblocks `METRICS_EVENT` when `metricsUrl` is `"postMessage"`.

Echoes are tagged `isGuestToHostEcho: true` and dropped on receive only for genuine same-window self-posts, so bidirectional types like `UPDATE_HASH` are not executed as host commands and a parent cannot suppress a command by forging the field. The echo uses `"/"`, postMessage's same-origin target, instead of `location.origin`, which throws in opaque-origin (sandboxed) frames. The same-window copy is posted before the parent post so a throwing parent target cannot skip the in-window host. The `GUEST_READY` self-post that shipped in 1.58.1 now carries the same additive marker. `IS_GUEST_TO_HOST_ECHO` and `GuestToHostEnvelope` are exported from `@streamlit/lib`.

Hosts that observe both the app window and the parent frame should ignore copies whose own `isGuestToHostEcho` is `true` to avoid double-counting. In-iframe-only hosts must not drop tagged copies — those copies are their delivery path.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #16644

## Testing Plan

resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16632: [fix] Prevent markdown lists from overflowing narrow containers.

related_pr.title: [fix] Prevent markdown lists from overflowing narrow containers
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes Removes `width: fit-content` from top-level markdown lists, so a list item holding a long unbreakable token wraps instead of spilling out of its container. `fit-content` resolves to `min(max-content, max(min-content, available))`, so it is floored at min-content. The markdown container's `overflow-wrap: break-word` is inherited by the list but, per CSS Text, `break-word` does not reduce intrinsic min-content width (`anywhere` does). So the `
    ` was sized to its widest unbreakable token — a file path, in the reported case — and never got a width to wrap within, computing to 304.81px whether its container was 134px or 704px. The sibling `

    ` has `width: auto`, fills the container and wraps, which is why the prose looked fine while only the bullets spilled. Regressed in **1.52.0** by #13036 (`text_alignment`), which introduced the whole `& > ul, & > ol` rule. Confirmed three ways: the rule is absent from the 1.51.0 wheel's static JS and present verbatim in 1.52.0's; the same app wraps on 1.51.0 (182px list in a 182px container) and does not on 1.52.0 (305px); and overriding only `width: auto` on 1.52.0 restores 1.51.0 geometry exactly. **Why deleting rather than capping.** The first approach here was to keep `fit-content` and add `max-width: 100%`. That works, but it only neutralizes a declaration that turns out to do nothing: `text-align` cannot position a block-level box, and the `

      ` has no auto margins, so the shrink-wrap never aligned anything. Measured left inset is 0 at every `text_alignment` value, and 0 for every `horizontal_alignment` value in a flex container, with and without `fit-content` — flex alignment positions the markdown element container, not the list. #13036's own description says "tables and lists within the markdown will always be left-aligned", so this removes a vestige rather than a feature. `display: block` was removed for the same reason: it is the UA default for `ul`/`ol`, and no reset in the repo overrides it. **Blast radius was wider than the report.** Neither the expander nor the sidebar was required — any container narrower than the longest list item overflowed. Also fixed: `st.columns`, `st.info`/`st.warning`, `st.chat_message`, `st.form`, `st.tabs`, `st.container(horizontal=True)`, `st.caption`, and — inside a list item — an inline `st.badge` that was clipped and could never engage its own ellipsis, a code block whose `
      ` scroller existed but did not scroll because the pre itself was stretched, and display math that was clipped by an `overflow: hidden` ancestor and unreachable entirely.

**One behavior change to be aware of:** a user-supplied background or border on a raw `
        ` (via `unsafe_allow_html` or injected CSS) now paints across the container instead of hugging the text, since the list is no longer shrink-wrapped. This makes a raw `
          ` behave like every other block element.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

Closes #16618

## Testing Plan

- **E2E Tests** — new `test_long_word_in_list_does_not_overflow_container` in `st_markdown_test.py`, with a 150px bordered container holding a `ul` and an `ol` whose items exceed it. Asserts each long item wraps (taller than the single-line sibling), each list stays within its markdown container, and — as the negative check — that no descendant leaves the container horizontally. Verified to fail when `width: fit-content` is restored (`AssertionError: Long list item did not wrap onto a second line`), and to pass on chromium, firefox and webkit.
- **No unit test** — jsdom has no layout engine, so min-content flooring is not observable in Vitest; the only assertable thing would restate the deleted declaration. Matches the precedent of #12370, the analogous fix for #12366.
- **Manual testing** — verified the reported repro, plus a sweep of the contexts above and an adversarial pass (250-char tokens, zero-break-opportunity tokens, CJK, RTL, emoji runs, 5-level nesting with long tokens at every level, `columns([1,20])`, `width=100`, `width="content"`, task lists, 60-item lists, popover/dialog/tooltip) in light, dark and mobile. `text_alignment` left/center/right/justify over paragraphs, tables and flat/nested/ordered lists is geometrically unchanged.
- **Snapshots** — `st_markdown-long_word_in_list` needs linux baselines generated via the `update-snapshots` label. Note that CI's comparison against the existing `st_markdown-text_alignment_*` baselines (which predate this branch and encode pre-fix nested-list rendering) is the real check that this is pixel-neutral.

By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license.

> **Medium Risk**
> Broad markdown layout change across many container types; low security impact but possible subtle visual differences (e.g. raw HTML list backgrounds spanning full width).
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **gh-16618** by changing how top-level markdown lists are sized so long unbreakable tokens (e.g. file paths) **wrap inside** narrow containers instead of overflowing.
> 
> In `StreamlitMarkdown` styles, **`width: fit-content`** and redundant **`display: block`** rules on `& > ul, & > ol` (and nested list blocks) are removed. Lists now follow the markdown container width while **`text-align: left`** is kept for list text when `text_alignment` is center/right/justify.
> 
> **E2E:** A 150px bordered fixture (`long_word_in_list`) is appended at the end of `st_markdown.py`, plus **`test_long_word_in_list_does_not_overflow_container`** with font gating (`expect_font`), wrap/geometry checks, horizontal overflow via `scrollWidth`, and snapshot **`st_markdown-long_word_in_list`**.

title: `st.code` with large text is causing a RangeError
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

Using `st.code` with a large text (> 30MB) is causing a `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. 

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-11996)

```Python
import streamlit as st

LOREM_IPSUM = (
    """
Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur. Excepteur sint occaecat cupidatat non proident, sunt in culpa qui officia deserunt mollit anim id est laborum.
"""
    * 70000
)

st.code(LOREM_IPSUM, language=None)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run app.

### Expected Behavior

Shows the text correctly.

### Current Behavior

Runs into a frontend error:

```
ErrorBoundary.tsx:54 RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at processLines (react-syntax-highlighter.js?v=010628c8:541:56)
    at SyntaxHighlighter (react-syntax-highlighter.js?v=010628c8:640:20)
    at renderWithHooks (chunk-5QKKVA7G.js?v=d5264bfd:11596:26)
    at mountIndeterminateComponent (chunk-5QKKVA7G.js?v=d5264bfd:14974:21)
    at beginWork (chunk-5QKKVA7G.js?v=d5264bfd:15962:22)
    at beginWork$1 (chunk-5QKKVA7G.js?v=d5264bfd:19806:22)
    at performUnitOfWork (chunk-5QKKVA7G.js?v=d5264bfd:19251:20)
    at workLoopSync (chunk-5QKKVA7G.js?v=d5264bfd:19190:13)
    at renderRootSync (chunk-5QKKVA7G.js?v=d5264bfd:19169:15)
    at recoverFromConcurrentError (chunk-5QKKVA7G.js?v=d5264bfd:18786:28)
```

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.47.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: MacOS
- Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

- This line is causing the RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded if the tree is too big: https://github.com/react-syntax-highlighter/react-syntax-highlighter/blob/842b45ba9328cc232cf6d085e2e6db97291b797d/src/highlight.js#L277
- Using `wrap_lines=True` doesn't cause the issue.
- Maybe related to https://github.com/react-syntax-highlighter/react-syntax-highlighter/issues/357?
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16567: [fix] Skip syntax highlighting for very long code blocks (#11996).

related_pr.title: [fix] Skip syntax highlighting for very long code blocks (#11996)
related_pr.description:
## Describing the bug fix

`st.code` with a large enough string fails to render at all, showing `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. `react-syntax-highlighter`'s `processLines` recurses once per line, so a long-enough input exhausts the call stack.

**Line count is the driver, not byte size.** I measured this in the jsdom test environment rather than assuming:

| Input | Lines | Size | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| short lines | 110,001 | 3.0 MB | renders |
| short lines | 120,001 | 3.2 MB | **overflows** |
| short lines | 200,001 | 5.4 MB | **overflows** |
| 999-char lines | 10,001 | 10 MB | renders |
| 999-char lines | 20,001 | 20 MB | renders |

So 20MB across 20k lines is fine while 3.2MB across 120k lines is not. A guard on size would have been the wrong axis in both directions — rejecting large single-line input that works, and admitting smaller many-line input that does not.

The fix skips highlighting above `MAX_HIGHLIGHTED_LINES = 50_000` and renders the code unhighlighted instead. Degrading to plain text beats failing to render. The limit sits well below the observed 110k–120k boundary on purpose: the usable stack differs between Node and browsers, so I did not want to place it at the edge of what I could measure in one environment. It still leaves an order of magnitude of headroom over any realistic source file.

Line counting stops as soon as the limit is passed, so an oversized input costs no more to check than an ordinary one, and nothing proportional to the input is allocated — `split("\n").length` on a 20MB string would build a 20k-element array just to read its length.

One acknowledged trade-off: the fallback drops line numbers, because they come from the highlighter's own row structure. That is noted in a comment at the branch.

## Testing

Five tests in `StreamlitSyntaxHighlighter.test.tsx`:

- highlights normally at `MAX_HIGHLIGHTED_LINES - 1`
- falls back past the limit, keeps the full text, emits no `.token` spans
- **renders 200k lines without throwing** — the actual regression; this input threw before the guard existed
- still highlights 20MB spread over 20k lines, pinning the line-count-not-size behavior
- keeps the copy toolbar and focusability in the fallback

Mutation-verified: disabling the guard fails exactly three of these, including the 200k-line case, while the two "must still highlight" tests correctly pass either way.

`make frontend-lint` and `make frontend-format` clean.

One note for the reviewer: `make frontend-types` reports 4 pre-existing `TimeInput.format` errors in my local checkout. They reproduce on clean `develop` with my changes stashed, and the regenerated `proto.d.ts` does declare that field, so it looks like local proto resolution rather than anything in this diff.

---

**Issue:** Fixes #11996

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Scoped UI guard with graceful degradation in the code block component; no auth, data, or API changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#11996**, where very large `st.code` inputs could fail to render with a stack/`apply` overflow inside `react-syntax-highlighter`.
> 
> **`StreamlitSyntaxHighlighter`** now counts lines with **`exceedsLineLimit`** (stops early, no `split`) and skips highlighting when input exceeds **`MAX_HIGHLIGHTED_LINES` (50,000)**. Over-limit content is shown via **`StyledCode`** (`stCodeUnhighlighted`) with full text, optional **`wrapLines`**, and the copy toolbar; **syntax highlighting and line numbers** are omitted on that path.
> 
> Tests cover the line-limit helper, normal highlighting under the cap, fallback past the cap (including 200k-line regression), large payloads with few lines still highlighted, **`wrapLines`** fallback styling, and copy toolbar presence.
>
