title: `st.data_editor` doesn’t return the input value unless you press Enter or click outside the editor
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

Unlike `st.number_input`, `st.text_area`, and other widgets, `st.data_editor` only returns the input value after the user presses Enter or clicks outside the currently focused cell (excluding clicks on buttons).

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7868)

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

def set_state(i: int, df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:
    st.session_state.stage = i
    st.session_state.df = df

if "stage" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.stage = 0

if st.session_state.stage == 0:
    st.write("Input your data")
    df = st.data_editor(pd.DataFrame({"col1": ["a", "b"], "col2": ["c", "d"]}))
    st.button(
        "Begin",
        on_click=set_state,
        args=[1, df],
    )

if st.session_state.stage == 1:
    st.write("Your data")
    st.dataframe(st.session_state.df)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click and edit a cell
2. Press the `Begin` button without clicking another area or pressing the Enter key.
3. Input value is not shown (input value is not returned from `st.data_editor`)

![Screen Recording 2023-12-22 at 2 02 09](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/45100960/0bd9f592-772c-440f-b06c-c73eee2e55c2)

### Expected Behavior

Input value is shown after clicking the button (input value is returned from `st.data_editor`).

### Current Behavior

Input value is not shown after clicking the button (input value is not returned from `st.data_editor`).

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:
  - 1.29.0
- Python version:
  - 3.11.6
- Operating System:
  - Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS
- Browser:
  - Google Chrome

### Additional Information

If this is an expected behavior, feel free to close this issue.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16132: [fix] Commit open data_editor cell edit on outside click.

related_pr.title: [fix] Commit open data_editor cell edit on outside click
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Editing a `st.data_editor` cell and then clicking an element outside the grid (e.g. an `st.button`) discarded the in-progress edit: the outside click triggered a rerun before the 150ms-debounced edit sync had run, so the pre-edit value was sent to the backend.

- Adds a `flush()` control to the `useDebouncedCallback` hook that runs a pending callback immediately and cancels its timer.
- Wires glide-data-grid's `isOutsideClick`/`onFinishedEditing` in the data editor to flush the pending edit synchronously on outside clicks. All other close paths (Enter/Tab/Escape, clicks inside the grid) keep the normal debounce, so rapid edits are still batched.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7868

## Testing Plan

- Unit Tests (JS): `useDebouncedCallback.test.ts` covers the new `flush` behavior; `DataFrame.test.tsx` covers flushing on outside clicks vs. staying debounced on other close paths.
- E2E Tests: `st_data_editor_editing_test.py::test_clicking_button_commits_open_cell_editor` opens a cell editor, edits it, clicks a button, and asserts the edited value is committed.

title: st.selectbox fuzzy search only matches contiguous substrings since 1.59.0 (BaseWeb → react-aria migration)
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

Since 1.59.0 (the `BaseWeb` → react-aria `ComboBox` migration, #15438), typing in
`st.selectbox` only matches options where the query is a **contiguous substring**
of the label. In 1.58.0 the search was truly fuzzy (non-contiguous subsequence),
so e.g. typing `ape` matched both `Grape` and `Apple`. Now it only matches
`Grape`, and queries like `aple` / `rp` that used to match return "No results".

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

FRUITS = ["Apple", "Apricot", "Banana", "Cherry", "Grape", "Mango", "Peach", "Pear"]
v = st.selectbox("Fruit", FRUITS, index=2)  # Banana pre-selected
st.write("value:", v)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above.
2. Click the selectbox and type `ape`.
3. Observe the dropdown.
4. Repeat with `aple` and `rp`.

### Expected Behavior

Fuzzy (non-contiguous, case-insensitive, label-only, score-ordered) matching, as
in 1.58.0:

| Type | Dropdown |
|------|----------|
| `ape`  | `Grape`, `Apple` |
| `aple` | `Apple` |
| `rp`   | `Grape` |

### Current Behavior

Only contiguous-substring matches survive (1.59.0 through current):

| Type | Dropdown |
|------|----------|
| `ape`  | `Grape` only |
| `aple` | *No results* |
| `rp`   | *No results* |

Root cause appears to be that the react-aria `ComboBox` applies its own built-in
`contains` text filter on top of Streamlit's already-fuzzy-filtered options, so
the visible list is the intersection (substring-only). Streamlit's own
`fuzzyFilterSelectOptions` util is still correct in isolation
(`ape → [Grape, Apple]`), so the fuzzy result is being re-filtered away by the
component. Consider disabling the component's built-in filter (e.g. a pass-through
`defaultFilter`) so Streamlit's fuzzy filter is authoritative.

(Screenshots attached: `EVIDENCE_v1_58_0_gap1_type_ape.png` shows `Grape, Apple`
on 1.58.0; `EVIDENCE_branch_gap1_type_ape.png` shows `Grape` only on 1.59.0+.)

### Is this a regression?

Confirmed via bisect against official PyPI wheels: `ape` → `[Grape, Apple]` on
**1.58.0** (BaseWeb `Select`), `[Grape]` on **1.59.0** (react-aria `ComboBox`).
Identical in Chromium and WebKit. Introduced by #15438.

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (introduced); still present in current 1.59.x / dev builds
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Linux (browser-independent)
- Browser: Chromium and WebKit (both affected)

### Additional Information

- Related migration PR: #15438 (Remove `BaseWeb` for `selectbox`).
- Discovered during QA of #15996 (which fixes the separate type-to-search
  append bug #15985). This filtering regression is independent of that fix.
- `filter_mode="fuzzy"` is the default and the mode affected; `prefix` / `contains`
  behave as documented.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16009: Fix st.selectbox fuzzy search only matches contiguous substrings since 1.59.0.

related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Fixes the 1.59.0 regression where `st.selectbox` fuzzy search only matched contiguous substrings.

Since the BaseWeb → react-aria `ComboBox` migration (#15438), RAC applied its own default `contains` text filter on top of Streamlit's `fuzzyFilterSelectOptions` result, so the visible list was the intersection (substring-only). Streamlit's fuzzy matcher was still correct in isolation.

The fix passes a no-op `defaultFilter` to `<ComboBox>` so Streamlit's own filter (fuzzy / contains / prefix / none) is authoritative and the already-filtered `displayOptions` reach the ListBox unchanged. Per the [React Aria docs](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/ComboBox.html#custom-filtering), `defaultFilter` is the documented way to override the built-in filter.

Restores 1.58.0 behavior:

| Type | Dropdown |
| --- | --- |
| `ape` | `Grape`, `Apple` |
| `aple` | `Apple` |
| `rp` | `Grape` |

related_pr.title: [fix] Clear stale AppTest elements on rerun
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

`LocalScriptRunner` now clears its `ForwardMsgQueue` on each `SCRIPT_STARTED` event, mirroring `AppSession._clear_queue`. Previously the queue accumulated deltas across internal reruns (`st.rerun`, page switches), so the parsed `AppTest` element tree kept stale/duplicate widgets from earlier runs.

- Fixes `KeyError` / "We'll never get here" `session_state` crashes when elements are dynamically added or removed across reruns.
- `fragment_ids_this_run` is forwarded to `clear()` so fragment-scoped reruns keep preserving deltas outside the running fragment (matching production).

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #12566
- Closes #9128

## Testing Plan

- `lib/tests/streamlit/testing/app_test_test.py` — Added `test_dynamic_widget_does_not_duplicate_on_rerun` (#12566) and `test_removed_widget_does_not_persist_on_rerun` (#9128). Both verified to fail on `develop` without the fix.

The example code demonstrates this with a single file. One would need to extract the string into a separate file to try the application through a browser.

```Python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest
```

## Describe your changes

title: st.selectbox Escape no longer clears the typed search query since 1.59.0 (stale query left in the input)
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

Since 1.59.0 (the `BaseWeb` → react-aria `ComboBox` migration, #15438), pressing
`Escape` while searching in a value-selected `st.selectbox` no longer discards the
typed query. The dropdown closes and the committed value is (correctly) preserved,
but the half-typed query stays visible in the input, so the box shows a query that
does not match the actual value. In 1.58.0, `Escape` cleared the query and
restored the committed value.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

FRUITS = ["Apple", "Apricot", "Banana", "Cherry", "Grape", "Mango", "Peach", "Pear"]
v = st.selectbox("Fruit", FRUITS, index=2)  # Banana pre-selected
st.write("value:", v)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above (value is `Banana`).
2. Click the selectbox and type `gr`.
3. Press `Escape`.
4. Look at what the input shows vs. the committed value.
5. (Control) Repeat steps 2–3 but click elsewhere instead of pressing Escape.

### Expected Behavior

`Escape` discards the query and restores the committed value in the input (as in
1.58.0): after Escape the box shows `Banana` again and `value` is still `Banana`.

### Current Behavior

- The dropdown closes and the committed value stays `Banana` (good — no accidental
  commit), **but the input still shows the stale query** (`gr`; on raw 1.59.0 the
  original append bug makes it `Bananagr`).
- Typing again without blurring appends to the stale query (e.g. `gr` + `ap` → `grap`).
- The control case (click away / blur) **does** correctly restore `Banana`, so only
  the Escape path is affected.

(Screenshots attached: `EVIDENCE_branch_gap2_after_escape.png` shows the stale
`gr` after Escape on 1.59.0+; `EVIDENCE_v1_58_0_gap2_after_escape.png` shows the
input restored on 1.58.0.)

### Is this a regression?

Confirmed via bisect against official PyPI wheels: after typing `gr` and pressing
Escape, the input is cleared/restored on **1.58.0** (BaseWeb `Select`) but retains
`gr` / `Bananagr` on **1.59.0** (react-aria `ComboBox`). Identical in Chromium and
WebKit. Introduced by #15438.

### Debug info
- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (introduced); still present in current 1.59.x / dev builds
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Linux (browser-independent)
- Browser: Chromium and WebKit (both affected)

### Additional Information

- Related migration PR: #15438 (Remove `BaseWeb` for `selectbox`).
- Discovered during QA of #15996 (which fixes the separate type-to-search append
  bug #15985). This Escape regression is independent of that fix.
- Likely fix: on `Escape` for a non-clearable selectbox, reset `inputValue` to the
  committed label and clear the active-filter state (mirroring the existing
  blur-restore path). Clearable (`index=None`) selectboxes already clear to `None`
  on Escape via a separate code path and are not affected.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16088: [fix] Escape now clears typed search query in st.selectbox.

related_pr.title: [fix] Escape now clears typed search query in st.selectbox
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Since 1.59.0 (BaseWeb → react-aria migration), pressing Escape in `st.selectbox` no longer restored the committed label when the user was typing a filter — the typed query stayed stuck in the input.

The capture-phase `onKeyDown` in `Selectbox.tsx` only handled Escape when the input was clearable AND had a committed value. It had no branch for the "user is actively typing a filter" case, and RAC can't restore the committed label from our controlled `inputValue` on its own.

Fix: add a branch that clears the active filter and re-syncs `inputValue` from the currently selected option when Escape is pressed with a non-empty filter. The existing clear-on-Escape contract is preserved (that branch only fires when the input is clearable and the query is empty).

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #16004

## Testing Plan

- Unit Tests (JS): 54/54 Selectbox vitest pass (3 new tests covering filter-active Escape)
- E2E Tests: new e2e case exercises the typed-then-escape flow
- Manual: verified in `make debug` that Escape restores the committed label without dropping focus

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized keyboard handling in the shared Selectbox component with explicit tests for the clearable Escape contract; no backend or auth changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **Escape** during type-to-search in `st.selectbox` so the input drops the filter query and shows the committed option again, without firing `onChange` or changing the widget value (#16004).
> 
> `Selectbox.tsx` now handles **Escape** in capture-phase `onKeyDown` when `filterActiveRef` is true: reset `inputValue` from the committed value, clear filter state, and close the dropdown. The existing **clear-on-Escape** path for clearable widgets runs only when the user is not actively filtering, so typing then Escape no longer clears the selection.
> 
> Coverage adds three Vitest cases (committed value, empty value, clearable without typing) and a Playwright regression for type-then-Escape.
>

related_pr.title: [fix] Popover in sidebar rendered off-screen
related_pr.description: When `st.popover` is placed inside `st.sidebar` and its content exceeds the space above or below the trigger, the popover body was clipping or force-flipping off-screen. Two problems fed the bug: 1. Floating UI's `shift`/`flip` middleware defaulted the boundary to the nearest clipping ancestor. Inside the sidebar that's `StyledSidebarContent` (`overflow: auto`). Since the popover body's `min-width` (20rem) is wider than the sidebar column, `shift` squished it and `flip` pushed it above the viewport once the bottom edge exceeded the sidebar's inner scroll boundary — even though the popover is portalled to `document.body`. 2. When the popover was taller than the space both above and below the trigger, `flip` picked the less-overflowing side but had no way to constrain height, so the popover extended past the viewport top. Fix: when `IsSidebarContext` is `true`, override the `flip`/`shift` boundary to `document.documentElement` (the `` element — `document.body` is `0×0` because `.stApp` uses `position: absolute; inset: 0`), and add a `size` middleware that clamps the popover's `maxHeight` to the available space at the chosen placement. The internal `overflow: auto` on `StyledPopoverBody` then handles scrolling. ## Screenshot or video (only for visual changes) Repro: sidebar with a popover containing ~11 sliders, viewport 1024×600. Before (slider 1 clipped above the viewport top): After (popover fits within viewport, internal scroll): ## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable) - Closes #9387 ## Testing Plan - Unit Tests (JS): 28/28 Popover vitest pass, no changes needed - E2E Tests: new `test_popover_in_sidebar_stays_within_viewport` asserts the body bounding box stays within the viewport AND extends past the sidebar's right edge (proving it escapes the clipping ancestor) - Manual: verified in `make debug` at 1024×600 that the popover body no longer extends off-screen and scrolls internally when content exceeds available space --- > [!NOTE] > **Low Risk** > Scoped to sidebar popovers via context; main-app popover behavior is unchanged when not in the sidebar. > > **Overview** > Fixes **sidebar `st.popover`** bodies clipping or flipping off-screen when content is taller than the space around the trigger. > > When `IsSidebarContext` is true, positioning now passes **custom Floating UI options** into `useFloatingOverlay`: `flip`/`shift` use **`document.documentElement`** as the boundary (so the portalled popover is limited by the viewport, not the sidebar’s `overflow: auto` ancestor), and an extra **`size`** middleware sets **`maxHeight`** from available space so tall content scrolls inside `StyledPopoverBody` instead of extending past the top of the screen. > > Adds Playwright regression **`test_popover_in_sidebar_stays_within_viewport`** (1024×600) asserting the popover rect stays in the viewport and still extends past the sidebar’s right edge. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c7e7cc18a7500dfcf3a3a2690bd598b73b960176. title: Widgets in an st.popover opened inside an st.dialog are occluded by the dialog and unusable
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

When an `st.popover` is used inside an `st.dialog`, the popover opens but its body
is rendered underneath the dialog's interaction layer. Widgets inside the popover
(e.g. a `selectbox`) cannot be interacted with, and clicking them lands on the
dialog's dismissable overlay — which can close the dialog. This is a regression
from the migration of `st.dialog` to React Aria (#15327); it worked in 1.58.0.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

@st.dialog("My dialog")
def show_dialog():
    st.write("dialog content")
    with st.popover("Open popover"):
        fruit = st.selectbox("Fruit", ["Apple", "Banana", "Cherry"])
        st.write(f"picked: {fruit}")

if st.button("Open dialog"):
    show_dialog()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app and click **Open dialog**.
2. Inside the dialog, click **Open popover** (the popover body appears).
3. Try to open the popover's `selectbox` dropdown and pick an option.
4. The dropdown does not open; clicking in the popover body instead hits the
   dialog overlay (and can dismiss the dialog).

### Expected Behavior

The popover body renders above the dialog and its widgets are fully interactive:
opening the `selectbox`, picking an option, and having the value commit —
dismissing neither the popover nor the dialog. (This is how it behaved in 1.58.0.)

### Current Behavior

The popover body is occluded by the dialog. The in-popover widget is not
interactable, and interacting with it can close the dialog.

Objective evidence (Playwright, both Chromium and WebKit): hit-testing the
in-popover selectbox at its own center with `document.elementFromPoint` returns
the dialog rather than the widget, and the dropdown cannot be opened even with a
forced click:

```
selectbox_hit = { topTestId: "stDialog", inBody: false, inDialog: true }
dropdown_opened = false
```

Root cause: the popover body is portalled to `document.body` (outside the dialog's
DOM subtree), while `st.dialog` is now a React Aria (`data-rac`) overlay that
establishes its own stacking/overlay layer that paints and hit-tests above the
portalled popover body. Control: a BaseWeb overlay opened from a widget placed
**directly** in the dialog (e.g. a `multiselect` in the dialog) renders correctly
above the dialog, so the dialog does not occlude all portalled overlays — only the
popover body at the `popup` z-tier.

### Is this a regression?

Confirmed via `git bisect` (probe: is the in-popover selectbox usable above the
dialog?):

| Commit | Description | Result |
|--------|-------------|--------|
| tag `1.58.0` (`209ad55c`) | 1.58.0 release (does not contain #15327) | PASS |
| `590deca9` | parent of #15327 | PASS |
| **`a7200715` (#15327)** | **Remove `BaseWeb` for `Dialog` (React Aria migration)** | **FAIL (first bad commit)** |
| `d65a3aae` (#15339) | Remove BaseWeb for Popover (floating-ui) | FAIL (not the cause) |
| current `develop` | — | FAIL |

#15327 shipped in 1.59.0 and is not in 1.58.0, which is why 1.58.0 works and
1.59.0+ is broken. This is independent of the `st.popover` floating-ui migration
(#15339). There is a prior related fix, #15876 "Fix React Aria dialog overlay
stacking", which does not cover this popover-in-dialog case.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: `develop` (reproduces on 1.59.0 and later; first broken in #15327)
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chromium and WebKit (both affected)

### Additional Information

- Scope: only the combination **popover inside a dialog** is affected. Standalone
  popovers, and widgets placed directly in a dialog, work correctly.
- Suggested direction for a fix: render/portal the popover body into the dialog's
  overlay/stacking context when it is opened inside a dialog, or raise the popover
  body to a tier that clears the React Aria dialog overlay (mirroring how direct
  BaseWeb overlays clear it via the `basewebOverlay` tier).
- Found during QA of PR #15961 (which fixes the separate #15959 popover-overlay
  stacking/dismissal issues). This popover-in-dialog gap is not caused by, and is
  out of scope for, that PR.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16067: [bugfix] Fix widgets inside popover-in-dialog being unclickable.

related_pr.title: [bugfix] Fix widgets inside popover-in-dialog being unclickable
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Widgets inside an `st.popover` opened inside an `st.dialog` were unclickable — clicks landed on the dialog instead of the widget. The popover's own dismiss behavior and any nested overlay (selectbox dropdown, date picker, etc.) were affected the same way.

**Root cause:** `@floating-ui/react`'s `FloatingPortal` (used by `st.popover`) creates its host `<div>` directly under `document.body`, which makes it a sibling of the dialog. React Aria's `ModalOverlay` (introduced in the dialog migration) applies `inert` to all siblings of the open dialog to enforce modal focus containment. The popover body's subtree becomes inert and loses hit-testing even though it visually renders on top of the dialog.

**Fix:** create a persistent portal host in `PortalProvider` tagged with:
- `data-react-aria-top-layer="true"` — opts the subtree out of React Aria's inert sweep
- `data-st-overlay-root="true"` — signals to dialog/popover dismissal handlers that interactions inside are "inside the overlay stack" (matches the existing pattern for the dataframe portal)

Route `Popover`'s `FloatingPortal` through this host via its stable `id`. Same shape as the existing dataframe overlay host.

Supersedes #16063 (fork PR — reopened from same-repo branch so CI runs with full permissions).

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #16005

## Testing Plan

- Unit test: `PortalProvider.test.tsx` verifies both portal hosts are mounted with the correct top-layer + overlay-root attributes and that the floating overlay host is a direct child of `document.body` (sibling of the dialog).
- E2E test: `test_dialog_allows_interacting_with_widget_in_popover` opens a dialog with a popover containing a selectbox, picks an option, and verifies (a) the widget is interactable, (b) the picked value renders, (c) the enclosing dialog stays open.
- Manual: reproduced with the exact snippet from #16005 before the fix (selectbox unclickable, `elementFromPoint` returns the dialog); confirmed working after.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches global overlay stacking and React Aria top-layer behavior for all popovers; risk is mitigated by matching an existing portal pattern and targeted E2E coverage, but could affect dismissal/stacking edge cases.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#16005**: widgets inside an `st.popover` opened from an `st.dialog` were unclickable because React Aria’s dialog overlay marks sibling DOM nodes `inert`, which broke hit-testing on the default `FloatingPortal` host under `document.body`.
> 
> **PortalProvider** now mounts a second body-level host (`stFloatingOverlayPortal`) with `data-react-aria-top-layer` and `data-st-overlay-root`, mirroring the existing dataframe portal pattern. **`st.popover`** routes its `FloatingPortal` through that host so the popover subtree stays interactive and clicks don’t dismiss the dialog.
> 
> Adds **unit** coverage on the new host’s attributes/placement and a **Playwright** regression (dialog → popover → selectbox).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e54e713b8b780b5ab9fcbf7a34d961f98993b683. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: Inconsistent margin above the first checkbox/toggle inside a horizontal container inside a column
description: ### Checklist ### Summary When putting checkboxes/toggles inside a horizontal container inside a column, a `margin-top: 0.5rem` is applied to the first checkbox/toggle, and not to the others. ### Reproducible Code Example [![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-13162) ```Python import streamlit as st cols = st.columns(2) with cols[0]: st.button("Button 1", width="stretch") st.button("Button 2", width="stretch") with cols[1]: with st.container(horizontal=True): st.checkbox("Checkbox 1") st.checkbox("Checkbox 2") st.checkbox("Checkbox 3") with st.container(horizontal=True): st.checkbox("Checkbox 4") st.checkbox("Checkbox 5") st.checkbox("Checkbox 6") ``` ### Steps To Reproduce Try the above code example. ### Expected Behavior Either the `margin-top: 0.5rem` should be applied to all checkboxes/toggles, or to none. I'm not sure if the `margin-top: 0.5rem` is still worth the trouble, since we now have `vertical_alignment="center"` as well as `st.space()` to align stuff perfectly in most cases, and considering this is the second bug I've found with it (see #10265). Given that `margin-top: 0.5rem` was broken not long ago, and remains broken in this new situation, I suspect not many people would notice if we removed the `margin-top: 0.5rem` altogether. ### Current Behavior A `margin-top: 0.5rem` is applied to the first checkbox/toggle, and not to the others. ### Is this a regression? ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.51.0 - Python version: 3.11.9 - Operating System: MacOS - Browser: Chrome ### Additional Information _No response_

related_pr.title: [bugfix] Fix inconsistent checkbox margin in horizontal container within column (#13162)
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes Fixes an inconsistent `margin-top` (and mirrored `margin-bottom`) on checkboxes when they are placed inside an `st.container(horizontal=True)` that is itself inside an `st.columns()` column. The alignment margin applied to the first-of-type / last-of-type checkbox in a TOP or BOTTOM aligned column was using a descendant selector, so it matched *any* first-of-type element container inside the column — including ones nested inside a horizontal container. As a result the first checkbox in each nested horizontal container was getting an extra `0.5rem` of `margin-top` while its siblings were not, producing visibly misaligned rows. Scope the selector to direct children of the column's own `stVerticalBlock` so the margin only applies to the intended direct-child checkboxes. ## Screenshot or video (only for visual changes) Before After: ## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable) Closes #13162 ## Testing Plan - **New E2E test**: added `test_column_top_alignment_does_not_leak_into_nested_horizontal_container` in `e2e_playwright/st_columns_test.py`, backed by a new "Vertical alignment - top with nested horizontal container" section in `e2e_playwright/st_columns.py`. related_pr.title: [bugfix] Include decorators in st.echo output
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

When a decorated function/class was the first statement inside `with st.echo():`, the `@decorator` lines were missing from the echoed source:

```python
with st.echo():
    @decorator
    def function():
        pass
```

...rendered just `def function(): / pass`. Adding any statement above the decorated node — even a bare string — happened to "fix" it, because the source range then started at that earlier statement's line.

**Root cause:** `ast.FunctionDef.lineno` (and `ClassDef`, `AsyncFunctionDef`) points at the `def`/`class` line — the decorators sit on the lines above. The existing code used `body[0].lineno` as the echo block start, which skipped the decorators.

**Fix:** for the first body node, use the min of `node.lineno` and each `decorator_list[i].lineno`. Single decorator, stacked decorators, and non-decorated first statements all take the correct start line.

Supersedes #16064 (fork PR — reopened from same-repo branch so CI runs with full permissions).

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #9252

## Testing Plan

- Unit test: `test_decorated_function_as_first_statement` in `lib/tests/streamlit/elements/echo_test.py` covers both a single-decorator function and a class with two stacked decorators as the first body statement. All 17 existing tests still pass.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized display logic in st.echo with a unit test; no auth, data, or runtime execution changes beyond correct source slicing.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`st.echo`** so echoed source includes **`@decorator`** lines when the first statement in the block is a decorated function or class (closes #9252).
> 
> Echo range start no longer uses only `body[0].lineno` (which AST sets on the `def`/`class` line). It now uses the **earliest line** among that node and its `decorator_list`, so single and stacked decorators are shown. Non-decorated first statements behave as before.
> 
> Adds **`test_decorated_function_as_first_statement`** for one-decorator function and two-decorator class cases.

title: One-click skills install (in-app nudge) fails ~12% on Windows via the symlink → GitHub-download fallback
description:
## Summary

The in-app one-click **"install skills" nudge** (added in #15473, shipping in 1.59.0) fails for a large share of **Windows** users. Internal usage telemetry shows the install-failure rate on Windows is roughly **10× higher than on macOS/Linux**, and the failures are **deterministic** (retries don't help). The cause appears to be the Windows symlink → GitHub-download fallback path in `install_skills`.

## Evidence (from internal usage telemetry, ~28-day window)

Among developers who clicked **Install** on the nudge, the share whose install ends in `skillsNudgeInstallFailed` (rather than `skillsNudgeInstallSucceeded`), broken down by the OS the app runs on:

| Server OS | install-failure rate |
|---|---|
| **Windows** | **~12%** |
| macOS | ~1% |
| Linux | ~0.5% |

Other cuts show **no** independent signal — the failures are Windows across the board:

- **Browser / browser version:** no effect beyond acting as an OS proxy (e.g. Safari, macOS-only, matches the ~1% macOS rate; Chrome, cross-OS, matches the Windows-heavy mix).
- **Python version:** flat (~8–14%) across every 3.10–3.14 build.
- **Streamlit version:** steady across 1.59.0 / 1.59.1 — not a regression in a single build.
- **Within Windows:** failure is broad (10–17%) across all Python/Streamlit/browser sub-segments — it's Windows generally, not a niche config.

The failures are **not** dropped-connection artifacts: cross-referencing against the `INSTALLED_SKILLS` page-profile field, developers whose install "failed" overwhelmingly do **not** end up with skills installed later (unlike the succeeded cohort), and they average multiple Install clicks without ever succeeding — i.e. retrying doesn't fix it.

Windows is the **majority** of one-click-install attempts, so this is the largest install audience failing at the highest rate.

## Root cause (code)

The only OS-specific branch in the installer is symlink support:

- `_install_skill_symlink` (`lib/streamlit/web/skills.py`) creates the skill as a symlink; on Windows without Developer Mode/admin, `Path.symlink_to` raises `OSError`/`NotImplementedError` and the function returns `False`.
- `_install_project_skills` then sets `symlink_failed` and **falls back to `_install_global_skills`**, which **downloads the skills archive from GitHub** (`_download_global_skill`) and copies it.
- That fallback raises `click.ClickException` on network/extraction errors, or `_conflict_error` if the global copy hits a pre-existing path.
- `InstallSkillsHandler.handle` (`lib/streamlit/runtime/backend_operation_handler.py`) catches the exception and returns it as `error_msg`; the frontend (`frontend/app/src/App.tsx`, `handleSkillsNudgeInstall`) then emits `skillsNudgeInstallFailed`.

So on Windows the install routinely depends on a **network download from GitHub**, and ~1 in 8 fail there — most plausibly blocked/failed GitHub egress in locked-down corporate Windows environments, or a conflict during the global copy. macOS/Linux create symlinks natively, never touch the network, and fail ~1%.

## Telemetry gap

The `menuClick` telemetry carries only the label (`skillsNudgeInstallFailed`), **not** the server's `error_msg`. So the failure can be localized to the Windows fallback path but the exact terminal reason (download blocked vs. extract error vs. copy conflict vs. hard symlink failure) can't be split from data. Emitting a reason code with the event would make this fully measurable.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Don't download from GitHub on the Windows fallback.** The bundled skills are already on disk in the installed `streamlit` package (`_get_source_skills_dir()`); when symlinks aren't supported, **copy from the local package** instead of fetching the archive from GitHub. This removes the network dependency that's failing.
2. Handle the global-copy conflict gracefully (treat an existing valid/Streamlit-owned skill as up-to-date rather than a hard error).
3. **Emit a failure-reason code** (and OS) with the `skillsNudgeInstallFailed` event so the sub-cause is observable end-to-end.
4. Align the nudge's show-gate detection (`detect_installed_skills`, marker-file based) with the installer's conflict check so developers the installer will deterministically refuse aren't repeatedly nudged.

## Repro

On a Windows machine **without** Developer Mode/admin (so `os.symlink` is unavailable), with an AI-agent harness present and Streamlit skills not installed, run any app locally and click **Install** on the skills nudge → the install fails (and retrying fails the same way).

## Environment

- Streamlit: 1.59.0+ (feature from #15473)
- OS: Windows (primary), any Python 3.10–3.14
- Local development, direct-loopback (the only context the nudge fires in)
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #16026: [fix] Bundle the skills meta-skill in the wheel; install it locally (no GitHub download).

related_pr.title: [fix] Bundle the skills meta-skill in the wheel; install it locally (no GitHub download)
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

The in-app one-click **"install skills"** nudge falls back to a **global** install when project symlinks aren't supported (Windows without Developer Mode). That global install **downloaded** the meta-skill from the `streamlit/agent-skills` GitHub repo, which:

- **failed ~12% of the time on Windows** (vs ~1% macOS / ~0.5% Linux) — deterministically, on locked-down corporate networks that block GitHub egress; and
- **tripped a security review** of runtime external downloads.

See #15933.

### Fix

Stop downloading. **Vendor the thin, version-agnostic meta-skill** (`SKILL.md` + `scripts/discover.py`, ~2 files) into the wheel and have `streamlit skills --global` **copy it from local disk**. This removes the network dependency entirely — fixing both the ~12% Windows failure and the external-download concern — while keeping the meta-skill's `discover.py`, which resolves each project's **version-matched** bundled content skills at runtime. So a single global install stays correct across Streamlit versions (the exact property a frozen copy of the content skill would lose).

> **Meta-skill vs content:** the *meta-skill* is version-agnostic (a router + `discover.py`); the *content* skill (`references/`, `assets/`) is version-matched and already ships in the wheel. Global mode installs the **meta-skill**; project mode still symlinks the **content**. We deliberately do **not** copy the content skill for global installs — that would go stale on upgrade.

### Changes

- **`skills.py`**: add `_get_meta_skill_dir()`; rewrite `_install_global_skills` to copy the meta-skill from the local package via the existing `_install_skill_copy`; **delete** `_download_global_skill`, `_GLOBAL_SKILLS_URL`, and the `urllib`/`tarfile`/`io` imports. Global-install targets are unchanged from `develop` (`~/.agents/skills`, plus `~/.claude/skills` when `~/.claude` exists).
- **Vendored** the meta-skill at `lib/streamlit/.agents/meta-skill/developing-with-streamlit/` (outside `.agents/skills/` so project-mode discovery/detection ignore it) and added a `package-data` glob so `scripts/discover.py` ships in the wheel.
- **CLI strings**: simplified the `--global` help and the global-install confirm prompt (dropped the download / local-copy phrasing — an implementation detail users don't need).
- **`discover.py` lint**: it ships to user machines, so it keeps the full ruff ruleset rather than a blanket per-file ignore — a file-level `# ruff: noqa: T201` (printing is its interface) plus line-level `S404`/`S603` on the two real violations.
- **Handler hardening**: forward only `click.ClickException` messages to the browser toast, so an unexpected `OSError` can't leak an absolute server path into the nudge.

The meta-skill is vendored **once**, and **`streamlit/streamlit` becomes the canonical source of truth** for it — maintained here and shipped in the wheel going forward. Its previous home, [`streamlit/agent-skills`](https://github.com/streamlit/agent-skills), is being deprecated and archived (README deprecation: streamlit/agent-skills#29).

## Testing

- Unit tests updated: removed the download tests; global-install tests assert the **meta-skill** (`SKILL.md` + `scripts/discover.py`) lands with **no network** — the no-network guard blocks at the socket layer, so any reintroduced download (urllib/requests/httpx) fails; added a **compatibility-contract** test that runs the vendored `discover.py` and asserts it resolves `<streamlit>/.agents/skills/developing-with-streamlit/SKILL.md` (pins `VIRTUAL_ENV` so it's deterministic outside `uv`); added a path-leak test on the handler; `package-data` glob + real-wheel-build guards confirm `discover.py` ships. **`skills_test.py`: 130 passed.**
- Ruff + mypy clean.
- Real CLI smoke test: `HOME=$(mktemp -d) streamlit skills --global --yes` installs both files with zero network; the installed `discover.py` resolves the bundled content `SKILL.md`.
- **Wheel build** confirms `scripts/discover.py` is packaged.

## Notes

**Streamlit is now the canonical source of truth for the `developing-with-streamlit` meta-skill** — it is vendored in the wheel here and maintained in this repo going forward. Its previous home, `streamlit/agent-skills`, is being deprecated and archived.

- Supersedes #15965 (which copied the *content* skill for global installs — the frozen-snapshot mistake this PR avoids).
- Telemetry (#15934) + nudge suppression (#15966) stay **parked** — revive only if the 1.60+ install-error rate stays >~1%.

### Action items (rollout)

Fixes #15933

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes are localized to optional agent-skills CLI/global install and nudge error surfacing; no auth, data, or core runtime behavior beyond safer toast messages and offline global install.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Global `streamlit skills` install no longer hits the network.** The version-agnostic **developing-with-streamlit** meta-skill (`SKILL.md` + `scripts/discover.py`) is vendored under `lib/streamlit/.agents/meta-skill/` and included in the wheel via `package-data`; `--global` copies it from the installed package. The GitHub tarball download path (`_download_global_skill`, related URL/imports) is removed, addressing locked-down Windows failures and runtime external-download concerns (#15933). **`discover.py`** resolves each project’s installed Streamlit and points agents at version-matched bundled content skills at runtime.
> 
> **In-app one-click install** still uses project mode first (with symlink→global fallback on Windows); comments and error handling are tightened so only **`click.ClickException`** text is shown in the browser toast—unexpected errors (e.g. **`OSError`**) get a generic message so server paths don’t leak. User-facing install errors for missing bundled skills no longer embed absolute paths (details go to logs).
> 
> **Tests** drop download/tarball cases; global install is asserted offline (socket-level guard), packaging globs and optional wheel-build checks cover `discover.py`, and a contract test runs the vendored `discover.py` against the bundled content skill.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b37c821d48dea8b8c5f0e9be4069c7fc60c06152. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

## Describe your changes

A `number_input` inside `st.form` submitted the *previously committed* value on the first Enter press instead of the freshly typed one. `commitValue` only wrote the new value to widget state via a deferred React effect, while the Enter key handler submits the form synchronously in the same event — so the form was submitted before the effect ran.

- When the widget is inside a form, `commitValue` now also writes the committed value to the `WidgetStateManager` synchronously (after range validation). Writing to a form's widget state does not schedule a rerun, so this adds no extra reruns.

## Describe your changes

Fixes a Windows-only crash where the file-watcher observer thread died with `ValueError: Paths don't have the same drive` (from `os.path.commonpath`), after which hot-reload silently stopped detecting code changes.

- Route all watched-path comparisons through new `util.paths_are_same()` / `util.path_is_in_directory()` helpers that guard `commonpath` against the `ValueError` (paths on different drives can never be a child path).
- Normalize Windows extended-length paths (`\\?\C:\...` and `\\?\UNC\...`) to their standard spelling before comparing, so events reported with the extended prefix still match the watched file/directory.
- Exclude `__pycache__`, `.pyc`, and `.pyo` artifacts from the stable directory identifier to avoid spurious reloads from bytecode regeneration.

Non-Windows behavior is unchanged (`normcase` is identity and `commonpath` results are the same).

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #12731

## Testing Plan

  - `lib/tests/streamlit/watcher/util_test.py` — extended-length/UNC path equivalence, different-drive and different-file negatives, `commonpath` `ValueError` handling, and `__pycache__`/`.pyc`/`.pyo` exclusion.
  - `lib/tests/streamlit/watcher/local_sources_watcher_test.py` — extended Windows path matches a watched file and a watched directory.
  - `lib/tests/streamlit/watcher/event_based_path_watcher_test.py` — equivalent path spellings match the same watched file; different-drive event is ignored without crashing.
- The crash is Windows-specific; the OS-dependent logic is exercised on any platform by patching `env_util.IS_WINDOWS`.

related_pr.title: [fix] Restore type-to-search in st.selectbox
related_pr.description: - Closes #15985 ## Describe your changes Typing into an `st.selectbox` that already has a value no longer cleared the committed label to start a fresh search — the typed characters were appended behind the selection (select "Banana", type `ch` → input shows `Bananach`, dropdown shows "No results"). **Root cause:** The react-aria-components `ComboBox` rewrite (#15438), which first shipped in **1.59.0**, keeps the committed label as the controlled `inputValue` on focus with the caret placed at the end. The first keystroke is therefore treated as an *append*, and the fuzzy filter runs against the concatenated string, matching nothing. The old BaseWeb selectbox cleared the query when the user began typing. (Note: the reporter guessed #15870, but that dropdown-virtualization PR is only in dev builds and is not in stable 1.59.x, so it cannot be the cause.) **Fix:** In the ComboBox input change handler, detect when the user is typing over an untouched committed label and start a fresh search — replacing the label with only the newly typed character(s). The newly typed characters are extracted with a prefix/suffix diff against the committed label, so it works regardless of caret position and browser-specific focus/selection behavior. This preserves arrow-key navigation, Enter-to-commit, `clearable`, `accept_new_options`, `filter_mode=None`, and the mobile read-only path (all covered by existing tests). ## Alternatives considered - **`select()` the label on focus** (the "standard" select-all-on-focus). Simpler, but not cross-browser robust: WebKit/Safari places the caret on mouse-up after focus, which collapses the selection so the keystroke still appends (verified failing in the WebKit e2e run — input became `malefem`). The prefix/suffix diff is independent of selection behavior. - **Clear `inputValue` on focus and rely on blur-restore.** Deterministic, but the committed value visually disappears on focus and it risks fighting RAC's own focus/blur input reconciliation. ## Testing - Frontend unit tests (`Selectbox.test.tsx`): typing after focus replaces the committed label and filters to the match; and a browser-independent case that simulates a browser appending the keystroke behind the label (`Bananac`) still resolves to `c`. Both fail before the fix and pass after. - E2E Playwright test (`st_selectbox_test.py::test_type_to_search_replaces_committed_value`). Verified locally passing in both Chromium and WebKit; the full `st_selectbox` suite (66 tests) passes in both browsers. Repro: https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-15985

title: `st.selectbox` with many options (~16k) freezes on open in 1.59.0 — forced reflow in StreamlitMarkdown (regression from 1.58.0)
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

An `st.selectbox` populated with a large number of options (~16,000) becomes effectively unusable in **1.59.0**: clicking to open the dropdown freezes the main thread for ~25 seconds. During the freeze the widget is greyed out (stale/running state) and neither clicking nor scrolling works. The same code on **1.58.0** opens the dropdown in ~0.5 s and is fully responsive.

A Chrome DevTools performance trace of the open interaction shows the time is dominated by a **forced reflow / layout thrashing**, with the top contributing call frame inside **`StreamlitMarkdown`** (plus `useFloatingOverlay` from the dropdown). On 1.58.0 the "Forced reflow" insight does not appear at all for the same interaction.

This looks like a rendering regression in how selectbox options are rendered in 1.59.0 (each option appears to go through the Markdown renderer). The 1.59 changelog includes a "fix selectbox format_func object-identity" change (#15618) which touches this code path.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

# ~16k options, with a trivial format_func (mirrors a real destination-search selectbox)
options = [f"{40000 + i} - LOCATION NAME {i}" for i in range(16000)]

choice = st.selectbox(
    "Search destination",
    options=options,
    index=None,
    format_func=lambda o: o,
)
st.write(choice)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app above with **streamlit==1.59.0**.
2. Click the selectbox to open the dropdown.
3. Observe the widget greys out and the tab freezes for ~25 s (no click / no scroll).
4. Downgrade to **streamlit==1.58.0**, rerun, repeat: the dropdown opens in ~0.5 s and is responsive.

### Expected Behavior

Opening a selectbox with a large option list should stay responsive (as it does in 1.58.0 — ~0.5 s to open), without freezing the main thread.

### Current Behavior

On 1.59.0 the open interaction blocks the main thread ~25 s. Measured with Chrome DevTools (Performance):

- 1.58.0: interaction (INP) ~495 ms, no "Forced reflow" insight, widget stays interactive (white).
- 1.59.0: ~26 s of blocked main thread, "Forced reflow" insight ~4.4 s, top frame inside `StreamlitMarkdown` (+ `useFloatingOverlay`); widget greyed out / not clickable.

Reproduced with the minimal snippet above **in isolation** (no other app code): on 1.59.0 the selectbox never becomes interactive on open (stays greyed ~25 s); on 1.58.0 it opens immediately.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (vs 1.58.0 OK)
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: Windows 11
- Browser: Chrome
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

### Additional Information

The forced reflow is dominated by `StreamlitMarkdown` — each of the ~16k options appears to be rendered through the Markdown renderer, and combined with the dropdown's `useFloatingOverlay` (which reads layout geometry) this triggers heavy synchronous layout on open. Suspected related change: #15618 ("fix selectbox format_func object-identity"), which modified the selectbox option render path in 1.59.

title: RuntimeError: reentrant call inside _io.BufferedWriter when stopping server via Ctrl+C on Windows
description:
## Bug: `RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>` when stopping the server via Ctrl+C on Windows

### Summary

On Windows, when the Streamlit server is stopped via Ctrl+C (SIGINT), the signal handler calls `server.stop()` which tries to write a "Stopping..." message to the console via `click.secho` → colorama's `AnsiToWin32`. This can race with the asyncio event loop's `select.select()` → buffered write to the same console handle, causing a `RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>`.

### Error

```
RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>
```

### Full traceback

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "bootstrap.py", line 43, in signal_handler
    server.stop()
  File "server.py", line 529, in stop
    cli_util.print_to_cli("  Stopping...", fg="blue")
  File "cli_util.py", line 34, in print_to_cli
    click.secho(message, **kwargs)
  File "termui.py", line 690, in secho
    return echo(message, file=file, nl=nl, err=err, color=color)
  File "utils.py", line 321, in echo
    file.write(out)  # type: ignore
  File "_compat.py", line 543, in _safe_write
    return _write(s)
  File "ansitowin32.py", line 47, in write
    self.__convertor.write(text)
  File "ansitowin32.py", line 177, in write
    self.write_and_convert(text)
  File "ansitowin32.py", line 202, in write_and_convert
    self.write_plain_text(text, cursor, start)
  File "ansitowin32.py", line 211, in write_plain_text
    self.wrapped.flush()
  File "_winconsole.py", line 176, in write
    buf = get_buffer(b)
  File "_winconsole.py", line 112, in get_buffer
    out: Array[c_char] = buffer_type.from_address(buf.buf)
RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>
```

Note: the signal handler at `bootstrap.py:43` is invoked *inside* the asyncio event loop's `_run_once` → `select.select()` call, so the reentrant write happens while the loop is already inside a buffered I/O operation.

### Environment

- OS: Windows 10/11 (10.0.26200)
- Python: 3.11.3
- Streamlit: latest (reproduced via `aider --gui` which launches Streamlit)
- Virtual environment: No

### Root cause

The signal handler (`signal_handler` in `bootstrap.py`) runs synchronously inside the asyncio event loop's `select.select()` call. It calls `server.stop()` → `cli_util.print_to_cli("  Stopping...", fg="blue")` → `click.secho` → colorama `AnsiToWin32.write` → `wrapped.flush()` → `_winconsole.py` `get_buffer`. This writes to the same `_io.BufferedWriter` that the event loop may already be writing to, triggering CPython's reentrancy guard: `RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>`.

This is a race condition — it doesn't happen every time, only when the signal arrives while the event loop is mid-write to the console buffer.

### Suggested fix

Avoid writing to the console from inside the signal handler. Options:

1. **Set a flag in the signal handler and do the actual stop + console output from the event loop.** E.g.:
   ```python
   def signal_handler(signum, frame):
       # Don't do I/O inside the signal handler; schedule the stop
       loop.call_soon_threadsafe(server.stop)
   ```

2. **Wrap the `cli_util.print_to_cli` call in a try/except** to swallow `RuntimeError` during shutdown (less clean, but minimal change).

3. **Use `signal.signal()` with a coroutine-aware handler** that doesn't write to the console synchronously.

Option 1 is the cleanest — signal handlers should never do I/O.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #15949: Fix RuntimeError: reentrant call inside _io.BufferedWriter on Ctrl+C.

related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Stopping the server directly inside the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler can interrupt the asyncio event loop in the middle of a buffered console write. `Server.stop()` immediately prints `Stopping...` via `click.secho`, which re-enters the same `_io.BufferedWriter` and trips CPython's reentrancy guard (`RuntimeError: reentrant call inside <_io.BufferedWriter>`), mainly on Windows where colorama flushes the console handle on every write.

The signal handler now schedules `server.stop` on the running event loop with `call_soon_threadsafe`, so the shutdown (and its console output) runs as a normal loop callback instead of inside the signal handler. When no loop is running (e.g. direct invocation in tests), the previous inline behavior is kept.

- The original crash is a timing-dependent race (signal must land mid-write), so it cannot be asserted deterministically; the test instead pins the invariant that no console I/O happens inside the handler while a loop is running.

title: st.tabs: widget rerun inside a tab renders all tabs' content stacked below the page (regression in 1.59.0)
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

**Regression in 1.59.0** (1.58.0 is fine): when a widget inside an `st.tabs` tab triggers a rerun, the tab bar disappears and the content of **all** tabs renders stacked vertically down the page, as if the tabs container no longer exists. A browser reload restores the tabs until the next widget interaction.

Possibly related to the tabs DOM rework in 1.59.0: in 1.58.0 each tab renders a `[data-baseweb="tab-panel"]` element (4 tabs → 4 panels, 1 visible); in 1.59.0 those elements are gone entirely.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

st.title("Tabs regression repro")

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
df = pd.DataFrame({"x": range(20), "y": rng.rand(20)})

def tab_content(name: str) -> None:
    st.metric("Metric", name)
    st.dataframe(df.head(3))
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df).mark_bar().encode(x="x:O", y="y:Q"), use_container_width=True)
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df).mark_line().encode(x="x:O", y="y:Q"), use_container_width=True)
    st.subheader("Leaderboard")
    choice = st.selectbox("Date range", ["A", "B", "C"], key=f"{name}_sel")
    n = {"A": 5, "B": 10, "C": 15}[choice]
    st.altair_chart(alt.Chart(df.head(n)).mark_bar().encode(x="y:Q", y="x:O"), use_container_width=True)

names = ["All", "Indy", "Clarksville", "Fort Wayne"]
for tab, name in zip(st.tabs(names), names):
    with tab:
        tab_content(name)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. `pip install streamlit==1.59.0 altair` and run the app above.
2. Stay on the first tab ("All").
3. Change the "Date range" selectbox from "A" to "B".

### Expected Behavior

The rerun re-renders the first tab's content in place; the other three tabs stay hidden behind the tab bar (this is the 1.58.0 behavior).

### Current Behavior

After the rerun the tab bar vanishes and the content of all four tabs is appended down the page in sequence. Measured headlessly (Playwright, counting `[data-testid="stVegaLiteChart"]` elements with a non-null `offsetParent`): 3 charts visible before the selectbox change, all 12 visible after. The same script against 1.58.0 shows 3 before / 3 after.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.59.0 (broken), 1.58.0 (works)
- Python version: 3.11
- Operating System: reproduced on both macOS 15 and Raspberry Pi OS (Linux/arm64)
- Browser: Chrome, and headless Chromium via Playwright

related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Drive `st.tabs` panel visibility from Streamlit's own active-tab state instead of React Aria's `inert` attribute, fixing a 1.59.0 regression where a widget-triggered rerun inside a tab made every tab's content visible and stacked down the page (the tab bar disappeared until a full page reload).

- `StyledTabPanel` now hides inactive force-mounted panels via `display: none` keyed on an `$isActive` prop (the same state that drives RAC's `selectedKey`), and the old `&[inert] { display: none }` rule is removed. RAC drops `inert` from inactive panels when their content re-renders on a rerun, which was the root cause; owning visibility ourselves mirrors how the pre-migration BaseWeb implementation hid panels from its controlled `activeKey`.

- Closes #15892
- Closes #15893

- `frontend/lib/src/components/elements/Tabs/Tabs.test.tsx` — asserts all panels stay mounted but only the active one is visible.
- `e2e_playwright/st_tabs_test.py` — `test_widget_rerun_keeps_inactive_tab_panels_hidden` (ordinary tabs + sidebar tabs + a page-wide "visible panel count doesn't grow" invariant) and `test_nested_tabs_stay_collapsed_after_rerun`. Both reproduce the reported bug and fail when the fix is reverted.

## Describe your changes

Login works, and st.secrets["auth"]["expose_tokens"] is available inside the app, but st.user.tokens.to_dict() remains empty.

```Python
    secrets={
        "auth": {
            "redirect_uri": ".../oauth2callback",
            "cookie_secret": "...",

            "okta": {
                "client_id": "...",
                "client_secret": "...",
                "server_metadata_url": "...",
            },

st.login("okta")
st.write(st.user.tokens)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

`st.user.tokens.to_dict()` should return {"access": "..."}

### Current Behavior

`st.user.tokens.to_dict()` returns {}

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

**Environment**:
- Streamlit 1.59.0
- Python 3.11
- Auth provider: Okta

### Additional Information

**Codex analyse** :
issue is in streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_websocket.py.
expose_tokens is read once when the WebSocket handler is created:

def create_websocket_handler(runtime):
    expose_tokens = get_expose_tokens_config()
But with st.App(secrets=...), programmatic secrets seem to be merged later during app startup/lifespan. So the handler may capture expose_tokens=[] before the injected secrets are available.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #15865: [fix] Honor expose_tokens with st.App programmatic secrets.

related_pr.title: [fix] Honor expose_tokens with st.App programmatic secrets
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Fixes `st.user.tokens` being empty when auth is configured via `st.App(secrets=...)` instead of a `secrets.toml` file.

- The WebSocket handler read `expose_tokens` once at route-build time. With `st.App(secrets=...)`, programmatic secrets are merged later during the ASGI lifespan (after routes are built), so the handler captured an empty config and the connect-time token filter never populated `st.user.tokens`.
- Now `expose_tokens` is resolved lazily on each WebSocket connect, when secrets are guaranteed to be available. No behavior change for the file-based `secrets.toml` path.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #15856

## Testing Plan

- Unit Tests (Python): `lib/tests/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_websocket_test.py` — added `TestWebsocketHandlerTokenExposure` which builds the handler while `expose_tokens` is empty, then simulates secrets merged afterward and asserts the exposed token flows through to `user_info["tokens"]` (and non-exposed tokens are excluded).

title: `st.page_link` and `st.switch_page` don't raise errors when pointing to non-existent pages with the same pathname as a real page
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

In filing a feature request (#10570), I got a pathological bright idea that I just confirmed: `st.page_link` and `st.switch_page` will silently switch to a different page than they are given (if the app developer passes a nonexistent page that happens to have the same pathname as a page that does exist).

### Reproducible Code Example

All files in a flat directory:
```Python
#app.py
import streamlit as st

def home():
    "home"

def page1():
    "Callable page1"

pg = st.navigation([home,st.Page("page1.py", url_path="foo")])
pg.run()

if st.button("not_page1.py"):
    st.switch_page(st.Page("not_page1.py", url_path="foo"))
if st.button("callable page1"):
    st.switch_page(st.Page(page1, url_path="foo"))

st.page_link(st.Page(lambda x: None, url_path="foo"))
st.page_link(st.Page("not_page1.py", url_path="foo"))
st.page_link(st.Page(page1, url_path="foo"))
st.page_link(st.Page("foo.py"))
# st.page_link("foo.py") # Only this one throws an error
```

```Python
#foo.py
import streamlit as st

"foo.py"
```

```Python
#not_page1.py
import streamlit as st

"not_page1.py"
```

```Python
#page1.py
import streamlit as st

"page1.py"
```

### Steps To Reproduce

All links/buttons redirect you to the page `/foo` defined by `"page1.py"` in `st.navigation`, even though other pages were technically used in the commands.

1. From home, click any of the buttons on the page.
2. Click home in the left navigation.
3. Repeat

### Expected Behavior

Trying to switch or link to a nonexistent page should throw an error.

### Current Behavior

So long as _some_ page in `st.navigation` has a matching url_path, the officially registered page in `st.navigation` is used and the passed page is silently ignored.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:

### Additional Information

_No response_
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #15721: [fix] Validate StreamlitPage source matches registered page (#10572).

related_pr.title: [fix] Validate StreamlitPage source matches registered page (#10572)
related_pr.description:
## Summary

Fixes #10572. `st.switch_page` and `st.page_link` blindly trust `StreamlitPage._script_hash` (which is derived solely from `url_path`). When a user constructs a `StreamlitPage` that shares a `url_path` with a page registered via `st.navigation`, the hash collides and the request silently routes to the registered page — even when the source file or callable differs from what the user passed.

This PR adds a `_validate_registered_page` helper that, on a hash collision with a registered page, verifies the source matches:
- File-based pages must point at the same `script_path` as the registered page.
- Callable-based pages must not collide with a file-based registered page.

When no page with the given hash is registered (e.g., apps that don't use `st.navigation`), validation is skipped to preserve existing behavior. Two different callables sharing one `url_path` cannot currently be disambiguated — `PageInfo` only stores `script_path` (empty for callables) — so that edge case is out of scope.

resolution: Resolved by merged PR #15646: [fix] Prevent ESC from clearing st.multiselect selection.

related_pr.title: [fix] Prevent ESC from clearing st.multiselect selection
related_pr.description: ## Describe your changes Pressing ESC on an `st.multiselect` with a default wiped the entire selection instead of just dismissing the dropdown/popover. Root cause: `st.multiselect` renders baseweb's `Select`, which defaults `escapeClearsValue` to `true`. When the control is `clearable`, ESC on the closed control clears the value — even for widgets created with a `default`. The fix makes `escapeClearsValue` conditional so multiselect mirrors `st.selectbox`'s `clearable` rule: - **Has a default** → ESC preserves the selection (only closes the dropdown/popover). - **No default (clearable)** → ESC clears the selection to empty. ```tsx escapeClearsValue={element.default.length > 0 ? false : !disabled} ``` This matches `st.selectbox`, where `clearable = isNullOrUndefined(element.default) && !disabled` and ESC only clears when clearable. ## Screenshot or video (only for visual changes) ## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable) - Closes #15637 - Repro: https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-15637 ## Testing Plan - Frontend unit tests: ESC does not clear when a default exists; ESC clears when there is no default. - E2E tests: ESC preserves the selection for a multiselect with a default (plain and nested in `st.popover`), and clears the selection for a multiselect without a default. --- **Contribution License Agreement** By submitting this pull request you agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license.

title: selectbox always reverts to first item in the options if the options contain arbitrary classes and format_func is used
description:
### Checklist

### Summary

When the options given to selectbox are instances of arbitrary classes **and** a format function is used, the selected option always revert to the first option if another option is selected.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import NamedTuple

import streamlit as st

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MyDataClass:
    id: int
    name: str

class MyNamedTuple(NamedTuple):
    id: int
    name: str

class MyPlainClass:
    def __init__(self, id_: int, name: str) -> None:
        self.id = id_
        self.name = name

TypeToTest = MyDataClass
a = TypeToTest(1, "one")
b = TypeToTest(2, "two")
x = {a: "I", b: "II"}

def format_function(s: MyDataClass | MyNamedTuple | MyPlainClass) -> str:
    print(x[s])
    return s.name

s = st.selectbox("selectbox", [a, b], format_func=format_function)
st.write(s.name)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code above and try to select the second option.

### Expected Behavior

The second option is selected.

### Current Behavior

selectbox always reverts the selection to the first option.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.58.0
- Python version: 3.14.5
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Opera, Edge, Firefox

### Additional Information

- If you replace `TypeToTest = MyDataClass` with `TypeToTest = MyPlainClass` the problem also occurs.
- If you replace `TypeToTest = MyDataClass` with `TypeToTest = MyNamedTuple` the problem does not occur.
- If you remove `print(x[s])`, the problem does not occur.
resolution: Resolved by merged PR #15639: [fix] Keep selectbox selection when format_func depends on object identity.

related_pr.title: [fix] Keep selectbox selection when format_func depends on object identity
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Fixes a bug where a `st.selectbox` with custom-object options reverts to the
first option whenever a `format_func` performs an identity- or class-dependent
operation (e.g. a dict lookup keyed on the option).

**Root cause:** Streamlit deepcopies the stored widget value across reruns, and
when option classes are redefined each run, the stored value is an instance of a
*previous* run's class. Validation called `format_func` on that stale instance to
check option membership; an identity-dependent `format_func` (like `x[option]`)
raises on the stale instance, so validation treated the value as invalid and
reset the selection to the default.

**Fix:** Selectbox now resolves the stored value against the current options by
its serialized *wire label* when `format_func` raises, instead of relying solely
on `format_func`:

- `RegisterWidgetResult` now carries `incoming_serialized_value` — the widget's
  stored serialized (wire) value, captured in `register_widget` before this run's
  serializer is applied.
- New `resolve_value_against_options` helper validates by `format_func` first and,
  if it raises, falls back to matching the stored wire label against the options.
  On a match it returns the *current* option instance (never the stale deepcopy).
- `selectbox` uses this helper, passing the captured wire label.

When neither `format_func` nor the wire label matches (e.g. options were swapped
to a different data model), the selection still resets to the default as before.

An alternative fix was prepared here: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15624
It was not chosen because it could lead to retaining invalid values in the edge case where the options list is updated. 

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

Fixes https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/15618

## Testing Plan

- **Unit tests (Python):** `TestResolveValueAgainstOptions` covers the resolver
  directly (value in options, reset, `format_func` raising with/without a matching
  wire label, and no wire label available). A new `selectbox_test.py` case asserts
  the selection persists with an identity-dependent `format_func`.
- **E2E test:** new `st_selectbox.py` case (selectbox 24) plus
  `test_keeps_selection_with_identity_dependent_format_func`, which verifies the
  selection survives both an interaction and a fresh rerun.

related_pr.title: [feature] Add `server.xsrfCookieSameSite` config option
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Adds a new `server.xsrfCookieSameSite` config option (`"lax"` default, `"strict"`, `"none"`) controlling the `SameSite` attribute of the `_streamlit_xsrf` cookie.

- Setting `"none"` automatically forces the cookie's `Secure` flag (browsers reject `SameSite=None` without it), so the XSRF cookie is delivered in cross-origin iframe contexts. This unblocks `st.file_uploader` (and the authenticated WebSocket handshake) when a Streamlit app is embedded on a different origin over HTTPS.
- Default `"lax"` reproduces the previous hardcoded behavior byte-for-byte, so existing apps are unaffected. Invalid values are rejected at startup with a clear error.
- Scope is intentionally limited to the XSRF cookie; auth cookies still use `SameSite=Lax`.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #9397
- Closes #5793 (cross-origin iframe facet; the auth-cookie and behind-proxy `Secure` aspects are out of scope here)
- Related #9719

## Testing Plan

- `lib/tests/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes_test.py` — XSRF cookie header generation: default `SameSite=Lax` (no Secure), `none` forces Secure (with and without SSL), `strict` does not force Secure, and the `same_site` argument of `_set_unquoted_cookie`.
- `lib/tests/streamlit/config_test.py` — option is registered, and `_check_conflicts` validation accepts `lax`/`strict`/`none` (case-insensitive) and rejects invalid values.
- No frontend changes. E2E coverage for the cross-origin embedded upload flow is recommended as a follow-up (`@pytest.mark.external_test`) since it requires an HTTPS-capable embedded host harness.

It works locally, and I suspect that this is caused by the _xsrf cookie not getting though, because I can see the cookie in dev tools locally, but not when deployed.

In particular, the cookie is missing the SameSite and Secure attributes.

### Reproducible Code Example

_No response_

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open any Streamlit app
2. Open browser developer tools

### Expected Behavior

Cookies have `SameSite=None; Secure` attribute.

### Current Behavior

_xsrf cookie is not transmitted when deployed on the cloud with SSO and HTTPS-only.

Locally this is what I am getting:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19314272/204801462-8a387f12-3df5-46e7-a9f6-69bd5293733d.png)

Plus the deprecation warning:

>Some cookies are misusing the recommended “SameSite“ attribute
>Cookie “_xsrf” does not have a proper “SameSite” attribute value. Soon, cookies without the “SameSite” attribute or with an invalid value will be treated as “Lax”. This means that the cookie will no longer be sent in third-party contexts. If your application depends on this cookie being available in such contexts, please add the “SameSite=None“ attribute to it. To know more about the “SameSite“ attribute, read https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie/SameSite

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.15.0
- Python version: 3.10, 3.11
- Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04 (WSL)
- Browser: Firefox, Chrome
- Virtual environment: yes

### Additional Information

This has been touched on in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/2517 and particularly https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/2517#issuecomment-1321281460. Feel free to close if you consider this is a duplicate, but I believe that the cookie configuration and Streamlit overwriting Jupyter's cookies are two different issues.

There are multiple reports of this on the forum:

https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/deployment-on-azure-ad-authentication-enabled-st-file-uploader-403-forbidden/30898

https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/azure-ad-xsrf-protection-and-st-file-uploader/33612

https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/deployment-on-azure-appservice-ad-authentication-enabled-st-file-uploader-403-forbidden/5839

https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/file-uploader-403-error-when-embedding-streamlit-app-in-iframe/24109

Whether they all have the same underlying cause, I cannot tell.

resolution: Resolved by merged PR #15634: [feature] Add `server.xsrfCookieSameSite` config option.

related_pr.title: [feature] Add `server.xsrfCookieSameSite` config option
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Adds a new `server.xsrfCookieSameSite` config option (`"lax"` default, `"strict"`, `"none"`) controlling the `SameSite` attribute of the `_streamlit_xsrf` cookie.

- Setting `"none"` automatically forces the cookie's `Secure` flag (browsers reject `SameSite=None` without it), so the XSRF cookie is delivered in cross-origin iframe contexts. This unblocks `st.file_uploader` (and the authenticated WebSocket handshake) when a Streamlit app is embedded on a different origin over HTTPS.
- Default `"lax"` reproduces the previous hardcoded behavior byte-for-byte, so existing apps are unaffected. Invalid values are rejected at startup with a clear error.
- Scope is intentionally limited to the XSRF cookie; auth cookies still use `SameSite=Lax`.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #9397
- Closes #5793 (cross-origin iframe facet; the auth-cookie and behind-proxy `Secure` aspects are out of scope here)
- Related #9719

## Testing Plan

- `lib/tests/streamlit/web/server/starlette/starlette_routes_test.py` — XSRF cookie header generation: default `SameSite=Lax` (no Secure), `none` forces Secure (with and without SSL), `strict` does not force Secure, and the `same_site` argument of `_set_unquoted_cookie`.
- `lib/tests/streamlit/config_test.py` — option is registered, and `_check_conflicts` validation accepts `lax`/`strict`/`none` (case-insensitive) and rejects invalid values.
- No frontend changes. E2E coverage for the cross-origin embedded upload flow is recommended as a follow-up (`@pytest.mark.external_test`) since it requires an HTTPS-capable embedded host harness.

title: Streamlit not detecting changes to multipage apps in WSL2
description:
### Summary

Streamlit isn’t detecting file changes in multi-page apps when I run it in WSL2 (Ubuntu 20.04).

I noticed that while it DOES detect changes to the main page, e.g. Home.py, it isn’t detecting changes to nested pages (e.g. a page in the pages directory), nor is it detecting changes to python modules that exist in the same parent directory (I confirmed that my python path includes the parent directory).

### Steps to reproduce

I created a minimal example [here](https://github.com/jonstrutz11/streamlit-minimal-wsl2-bug). You can follow the steps in the README.

I ran this example both in Windows (where changes to all pages and module were detected successfully) and in WSL2 (where changes to only Home.py were detected).

not for me, but I just started using streamlit recently

resolution: Resolved by merged PR #15562: [fix] Default to polling file watcher in WSL.

related_pr.title: [fix] Default to polling file watcher in WSL
related_pr.description:
## Describe your changes

Streamlit's `"auto"` file watcher relies on watchdog/inotify, which does not reliably receive file-change events across the Windows↔Linux filesystem boundary in WSL. As a result, edits often go undetected and the app never reruns.

- Detect WSL via `WSL_DISTRO_NAME`/`WSL_INTEROP` env vars and the `/proc/version` kernel marker (`env_util.IS_WSL`).
- When `server.fileWatcherType="auto"` and WSL is detected, use the polling watcher and print a one-time info message pointing to `fileWatcherType="watchdog"` as an escape hatch.
- Explicit `"watchdog"`, `"poll"`, and `"none"` settings are unaffected.

## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)

- Closes #5178

## Testing Plan

- `lib/tests/streamlit/env_util_test.py` — WSL detection via env vars, `/proc/version` marker, native-Linux negative case, and unreadable `/proc/version`.
- `lib/tests/streamlit/watcher/path_watcher_test.py` — `"auto"` uses polling (and reports once, without probing watchdog) in WSL; explicit `"watchdog"` still overrides the WSL default.
